findings.finding_text: Attrition is measured night-by-night rather than cumulatively, with a 90% threshold (versus CD's 70%), damages at 100% of gross room rate rather than 70% lost-profit, no credit for sold-out nights unless 100% occupied, and the hotel's records are made final, binding, and unauditable by Group. There is also no rebooking credit provision.
findings.cd_standard: Attrition should be measured cumulatively, triggered only below 70% of block, damages capped at 70% lost profit on the single net group rate for actually-unsold rooms, with full credit for any night at 95%+ occupancy, audit rights, and rebooking credit.
findings.proposed_language: Attrition liability, if any, will be calculated on a cumulative (not night-by-night) basis, with liability triggered only if Group's actual pickup falls below seventy percent (70%) of the total contracted room block. For each unsold room night below that threshold, Group will pay an amount equal to seventy percent (70%) (lost profit) of Group's single confirmed net group rate of $289.00 (plus tax), calculated as the lesser of the number of unsold rooms in the Hotel that night or the shortfall between Group's minimum block and actual pickup. For any night the Hotel achieves 95% occupancy or higher, Group will receive full credit toward its block commitment for that night. At Group's request, Hotel will provide its occupancy and registration records to verify the calculation, and such records shall be subject to audit by Group. Should a ConferenceDirect client rebook the Hotel within three years, Hotel will credit up to 100% of attrition damages paid toward the new booking.
findings.quoted_text: Attrition is measured on a night-by-night basis, with shortfalls calculated by comparing actual rooms occupied to the block size on each night of the event period. Group shall be deemed in attrition if actual occupancy falls below the attrition threshold of ninety percent (90%) on any night.
findings.exposure_basis: Worst case: 340 rooms/night x 4 nights x $289 = $393,040 max block revenue exposed to 100% damages if occupancy is even slightly below 90% threshold each night, versus CD standard 70% threshold at 70% lost-profit; illustrative gap using full block at 100% penalty rate versus a hypothetical 70%-of-70%-shortfall approach.

findings.finding_text: Hotel's occupancy records and calculation of damages are declared final, binding, and not subject to audit or verification by Group, eliminating any audit right.
findings.cd_standard: Group should have audit rights and a formula-based, not discretionary, damages calculation.
findings.proposed_language: Group shall have the right to review and audit Hotel's occupancy records, registration cards, and room-by-room occupancy logs, including at Group's request a joint or independent comparison against Group's registration list, to verify the Hotel's attrition calculations.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel's occupancy records, registration cards, and room-by-room occupancy logs shall not be open to Group for audit, verification, or inspection, and Group waives any right to independently verify the Hotel's calculations or to contest the Hotel's occupancy records on any basis.

findings.finding_text: The cutoff date is set at 45 days prior to arrival, exceeding CD's standard of no earlier than 21 days, and reservations after cutoff go to rack rate rather than continuing at group rate while rooms remain available.
findings.cd_standard: Cutoff should be no earlier than 21 days prior to arrival, and post-cutoff reservations should still receive the group rate as long as the hotel is selling rooms to the public or the room type is available.
findings.proposed_language: The cutoff date for the room block will be twenty-one (21) days prior to Group's arrival date. After the cutoff date, Hotel will continue to hold any unassigned rooms in Group's block if Group pays for them in full, refunding any amounts later paid by attendees for those rooms, or will release them to reduce Group's attrition liability after consultation with Group. Group members may continue to reserve rooms at the group rate for as long as Hotel is selling rooms to the general public, regardless of room type.
findings.quoted_text: Reservations for rooms within the block committed for the National Association of Coastal Engineers event shall be accepted by the Hotel only when received on or before forty-five (45) days prior to the arrival date of April 12, 2027.

findings.finding_text: Name changes are treated as new reservations at prevailing (non-group) rates rather than being permitted at the group rate; no-shows result in cancellation of the entire remaining stay rather than reinstatement for the following night; individual cancellations require 72 hours' notice rather than being free until 6pm day-of-arrival; and cancellations within 72 hours incur a full night's charge with no exception for emergencies.
findings.cd_standard: Name changes should be allowed at the group rate up to arrival; no-shows should be reinstated for the following night at the same rate; individual cancellation should be penalty-free until 6pm on arrival day (or 24 hours before, with emergency exception).
findings.proposed_language: Name changes may be made to room reservations at the group rate at any time up to and including the arrival date. An attendee who fails to arrive on the first night shall be reinstated for the following night at the same rate unless Group directs otherwise. No cancellation fee will be assessed for any room cancelled before 6:00 p.m. on the day of arrival, or in the event of a documented medical or personal emergency.
findings.quoted_text: A name change on any individual reservation shall be treated as a new reservation at the Hotel's prevailing rate for comparable accommodations on the relevant dates, and the attendee shall be responsible for any rate difference between the Group rate and the prevailing rate.

findings.finding_text: Cancellation damages are calculated on gross room revenue rather than 70% lost-profit on the net group rate, the hotel has no duty to mitigate/resell (proceeds retained entirely by hotel with no credit to Group), and there is no rebooking credit. The sliding scale tiers also run higher than typical (up to 100% at 30 days or fewer, but even 365+ days out is 25%).
findings.cd_standard: Cancellation damages should be based on 70% of lost room profit on the confirmed group rate applied to the block less allowable attrition, with mandatory resale mitigation credited against damages, and rebooking credit if a CD client rebooks.
findings.proposed_language: Liquidated damages will be calculated as a percentage of room profit (defined as seventy percent (70%) of the confirmed single net group rate of $289.00, multiplied by the final adjusted room block less allowable attrition) on the sliding scale set out below. Hotel will undertake all reasonable efforts to resell cancelled rooms and function space and will credit those revenues against the damages owed, not to exceed the full amount of such damages. Should a ConferenceDirect client rebook the Hotel within three years, Hotel will credit up to 100% of the damages paid toward the new booking's room revenue.
findings.quoted_text: Group shall be liable to the Hotel for liquidated damages calculated as a percentage of gross room revenue that would have been earned by the Hotel for all guest rooms for all nights within the event period of April 12-16, 2027, based upon the negotiated room rate and the full room block size.
findings.exposure_basis: Full room block gross revenue at risk: 340 rooms x 4 nights x $289 = $393,040 as the base for 100% liquidated damages tier, versus a 70%-lost-profit-based calculation under CD standard.

findings.finding_text: The hotel has no obligation whatsoever to attempt resale of released rooms/space, retains 100% of any resale proceeds with no credit to Group, and denies Group any right to review resale records or challenge mitigation efforts.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should have an affirmative, documented duty to resell canceled inventory, credit proceeds against damages, and make records available to Group; damages should not be due until 30 days after event dates pending evidence of mitigation.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will undertake all reasonable efforts to resell canceled rooms and food and beverage functions through all group and transient channels, and will credit those revenues against any cancellation or attrition damages owed by Group, not to exceed the full amount of such damages. Hotel will document its mitigation efforts and make records available to Group upon request. Cancellation damages, if any, are due thirty (30) days after the meeting dates, provided Hotel supplies reasonable evidence of its mitigation efforts.
findings.quoted_text: Upon release of any room inventory or function space by Group, whether through attrition, cancellation, or other reduction of Group's commitment, the Hotel shall have no obligation to attempt to resell such released inventory or function space, nor shall the Hotel be required to undertake any specific actions, marketing efforts, or promotional activities directed toward filling released space.

findings.finding_text: If the hotel wrongfully cancels, its liability is limited to a refund of deposits only, with an explicit waiver of consequential, incidental, and indirect damages, and Group must bear its own attorney's fees regardless of outcome.
findings.cd_standard: If the hotel cancels without a contractual right to do so, it should owe the group all direct, indirect, and consequential damages, including costs to find a replacement venue, rate/airfare differentials, and attorney's fees.
findings.proposed_language: In the event Hotel cancels this Agreement other than as permitted under this Agreement, Hotel will pay Group for all direct, indirect, and consequential damages, expenses, attorney's fees, and costs incurred by Group on account of such cancellation, including but not limited to staff time and travel expenses to secure an alternate location, incremental room rate and airfare differentials, function space rental, and communication, postage, and printing costs.
findings.quoted_text: In the event the Hotel wrongfully cancels this Agreement, the Hotel's sole obligation and the Group's exclusive remedy shall be the refund of any deposits paid by the Group to the Hotel, without interest and without liability for any other costs, losses, or damages incurred by the Group in connection with the event.

findings.finding_text: Force majeure is limited to events causing objective physical impossibility, explicitly excludes epidemics/pandemics, government travel advisories/restrictions, and attendee safety concerns; also requires only 48 hours' notice (procedurally fine) but retains deposits despite termination and provides no refund or waiver of fees for reduced-size events.
findings.cd_standard: Force majeure should allow cancellation where performance is illegal, impossible, commercially impracticable, or inadvisable (including health/safety), or would cause 20%+ attendee cancellations, and should explicitly include terrorism, disease/epidemics, government advisories and restrictions; deposits should be refunded promptly.
findings.proposed_language: Either party may cancel this Agreement without liability upon written notice should any cause beyond the parties' control — including acts of God, war, terrorism, disease or epidemic, CDC or governmental travel advisories, government closures or emergency declarations, or governmental, corporate, or educational travel restrictions — make performance illegal, impossible, commercially impracticable, or inadvisable (including for health or safety reasons), or cause or lead Group to reasonably anticipate cancellation by 20% or more of attendees. Hotel will refund all deposits and prepayments within five (5) business days of the notice of termination.
findings.quoted_text: Force majeure events are limited to occurrences such as war, acts of terrorism, earthquakes, floods, or similar extraordinary natural events that render performance of this agreement objectively impossible without regard to economic hardship, inconvenience, or increased cost.

findings.finding_text: Deposits are retained by the Hotel even where force majeure terminates the agreement, and no refund or credit is issued for prior payments.
findings.cd_standard: Deposits should be refunded promptly upon force majeure cancellation.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will refund all deposits and prepayments made by Group within five (5) business days of a force majeure cancellation notice.
findings.quoted_text: The invocation of force majeure by either party shall not relieve Group of its obligations to remit the deposit and initial payment to the Hotel, which shall be retained by the Hotel despite any termination of this agreement resulting from force majeure.
findings.exposure_basis: Security deposit of $25,000 retained by Hotel even upon force majeure termination.

findings.finding_text: The named storm clause forces forfeiture of the full deposit even when Group properly exercises its cancellation right, rather than a clean cancellation without penalty.
findings.cd_standard: Named storm clause should allow cancellation without liability, including refund of amounts paid, when a storm is forecast to affect the venue within the specified window.
findings.proposed_language: Should Group exercise its named storm cancellation right, Hotel will refund all deposits and prepayments made by Group within five (5) business days of the cancellation notice, without forfeiture.
findings.quoted_text: Should Group invoke the named storm cancellation right, Group shall forfeit the deposit paid to the Hotel, which shall be retained by the Hotel as partial compensation for the Hotel's lost revenue and costs incurred in preparation for the event.
findings.exposure_basis: Security deposit of $25,000 forfeited upon exercise of named storm cancellation right.

findings.finding_text: Termination for Hotel's uncured material breach does not relieve Group of liability — Group must still pay the Hotel's lost profit and consequential damages — and separately, any termination by Group for any reason (including for cause) is deemed a cancellation subject to the full liquidated damages scale, eliminating any no-liability termination right.
findings.cd_standard: Termination for cause should let the group walk away with no liability and a prompt refund, entirely separate from the cancellation clause's liquidated-damages scale.
findings.proposed_language: Group may terminate this Agreement without liability, and Hotel will refund all deposits and prepayments within five (5) days, upon Hotel's uncured material breach following thirty (30) days' written notice. Termination for cause under this clause does not trigger the liquidated-damages calculation in the cancellation clause.
findings.quoted_text: Notwithstanding the grounds upon which Group effects termination, whether for cause, convenience, or otherwise, any and all termination by Group shall be deemed and treated as a cancellation subject to the cancellation damages scale set forth in this Agreement.

findings.finding_text: Any F&B shortfall is billed at 100% of the difference rather than a fraction, and there is no provision counting affiliate/exhibitor F&B revenue toward the minimum. Menu pricing is locked 24 months out, which exceeds CD's 12-month standard.
findings.cd_standard: Shortfall should be billed at 35% of the gap, not the full difference; menu pricing should be locked no earlier than 12 months before the event; affiliate/exhibitor F&B revenue should count toward the minimum.
findings.proposed_language: Menu prices will be confirmed not earlier than twelve (12) months prior to the Event. If actual food and beverage revenue is less than the minimum, Group will pay Hotel thirty-five percent (35%) of the difference between actual revenue and the minimum. Food and beverage revenue from all affiliate organizations and exhibitors meeting in conjunction with Group's event will count toward the minimum.
findings.quoted_text: If Group's actual food and beverage consumption during the Event Period falls short of the minimum guarantee, Group shall pay the shortfall in full.

findings.finding_text: Gratuity and service charge are used interchangeably and not separately defined, with the Hotel retaining sole discretion over distribution and no commitment that any portion reaches staff as a tip. The combined 24% charge is also applied to room charges, not just F&B.
findings.cd_standard: Gratuity and service charge should be separately and clearly defined with stated percentages; gratuity should be fully distributed to staff who worked the event, while a separate service charge should be disclosed as hotel revenue; neither should apply to room rental or equipment already carrying a labor fee.
findings.proposed_language: [X]% of the food and beverage total will be added as a gratuity and fully distributed to the servers, bussers, and bartenders assigned to the Event. A separate service charge of [X]%, disclosed as Hotel revenue and not distributed as a tip, may also apply. Neither gratuity nor service charge will be applied to room charges, meeting room rental, or equipment already carrying a labor fee.
findings.quoted_text: A service charge and gratuity shall be added to all food and beverage, banquet, and room charges, and the terms 'gratuity' and 'service charge' shall be used interchangeably throughout this Agreement and are not separately defined.

findings.finding_text: The contract sets no minimum staffing ratios for servers or bartenders, leaves staffing entirely to hotel discretion, and imposes labor/bartender fees on all functions regardless of size rather than only for groups under 25.
findings.cd_standard: Contract should guarantee minimum staffing ratios (1 server per 25 at plated breakfast, 20 at plated lunch/dinner, etc.; 1 bartender per 75 hosted/100 cash) with no labor fee except for functions under 25 people.
findings.proposed_language: At all meal functions, Hotel will provide at least one server for every twenty-five (25) guests at a plated breakfast and every twenty (20) guests at a plated lunch or dinner, and one server for every forty (40) guests at a buffet breakfast and every thirty (30) guests at a buffet lunch or dinner, with no extra service or labor charge for these ratios. Hotel will provide one bartender for every seventy-five (75) guests at hosted bars and one for every one hundred (100) guests at cash bars, with no bartender fees. No special labor fee will apply except for functions of fewer than twenty-five (25) people.
findings.quoted_text: Staffing at food and beverage functions, including the assignment of servers, bartenders, runners, and other service personnel, is at the Hotel's discretion and shall be determined by the Hotel based on the number of attendees, the complexity of the menu, the duration of the function, and the Hotel's operational requirements.

findings.finding_text: No function space is named or reserved in the agreement (space is only 'tentative' per Exhibit A pending signature, then subject to unilateral reassignment), room rental is charged rather than waived, and no in-room equipment (mic, podium, power, lighting, HVAC) is guaranteed at no charge.
findings.cd_standard: Function rooms should be named with minimum square footage/ceiling height, changeable only by mutual written consent, with room rental waived and each room provided with a wired microphone, podium, power, lighting, and HVAC at no charge.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will hold the function space set out in Exhibit A, with room rental charges waived, and will specify minimum square footage and ceiling height for each space. No change will be made to function space assignments without the written consent of both parties. Hotel will provide in each meeting room, at no charge, one wired microphone, a podium, power, lighting, and HVAC.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel shall assign all function space for the Group's use during the Event at the Hotel's sole discretion, and no function room is named or reserved in this Agreement.

findings.finding_text: AV pricing is not locked at contracting and can be adjusted up to the event; complimentary internet and AV discounts are expressly conditioned on exclusive use of the in-house AV vendor, contrary to CD's standard that such conditioning is prohibited.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should honor AV/internet quotes attached at contracting with a minimum bandwidth guarantee, and use of the in-house AV provider should never be a condition for discounted or complimentary services like internet.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will honor the pricing of the attached audio-visual quote prepared at the time of contracting and will apply a stated discount to additional needs, regardless of provider. Hotel will provide complimentary internet with a minimum of 10 Mbps download/1 Mbps upload, and use of Hotel's in-house AV provider will not be a condition of any discounted or complimentary internet or other services.
findings.quoted_text: Complimentary internet access and any discounted or complimentary services relating to audio-visual provision, including concessions, upgrades, or technical support at no charge, shall be conditioned upon the Group's exclusive use of the Hotel's in-house audio-visual provider for all function space during the Event.

findings.finding_text: The Hotel reserves an open-ended right to add fees at any time, including undisclosed ones, and Group waives any objection; a $35/night resort fee applies to every room including complimentary rooms, with no waiver for attendees.
findings.cd_standard: All charges must be disclosed in writing before signing; undisclosed charges should be waived outright; resort fees should be waived for attendees (or at least discounted/fixed) with services still honored.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will disclose in writing, prior to execution of this Agreement, all charges associated with the Event, including resort fees and surcharges. Any charge not disclosed to Group in writing prior to signature is waived. Hotel will waive the resort fee for all attendees, including those in complimentary rooms, while continuing to honor resort fee services.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel reserves the right to impose additional fees, surcharges, and service charges upon Group at any time, including without limitation after the execution of this Agreement.
findings.exposure_basis: $35/night resort fee x approximately 233 total room nights average occupancy or up to 680 total contracted room-nights (340 peak x roughly 2 average per night structure); using stated 4 nights x 170 rooms average = 680 room nights x $35 = $23,800 as a maximum illustrative exposure; using more conservative peak calc of 340 rooms x $35 = $11,900/night. Using total contracted room nights of 680 x $35 = $23,800 is the more defensible base, but leaving as null given ambiguity is safer — providing a calculable range instead.

findings.finding_text: The complimentary room ratio (1:75) is worse than CD's 1:40 standard, is characterized as a non-binding 'guideline' subject to the Hotel's sole discretion to reduce or withdraw, complimentary rooms are still charged all fees/taxes as if paid, and all comp room credits are forfeited entirely if the block is not 100% met.
findings.cd_standard: Complimentary rooms should be earned on a clear, cumulative, non-discretionary formula of 1 per 40 occupied room nights, not forfeited due to attrition already compensated elsewhere, with all occupied rooms counted including miscoded rooms and no-show/cancellation fee credits.
findings.proposed_language: Group will receive one (1) complimentary room for every forty (40) occupied, revenue-producing room nights actualized, calculated cumulatively across the entire room block, regardless of whether the contracted block was otherwise met. All occupied rooms will be counted toward Group's pickup, including any rooms credited through a room block audit and one room night for each no-show or cancellation fee charged. Complimentary rooms will not be subject to resort fees, service charges, or gratuities.
findings.quoted_text: The complimentary room ratio of seventy-five (75) stated above is a guideline only and does not create an entitlement in Group. The award and allocation of any complimentary rooms shall be at the sole and absolute discretion of the Hotel

findings.finding_text: The Hotel retains unlimited right to sell rooms below Group's rate with no rate-matching obligation; any rate adjustment applies only prospectively, is deemed non-commissionable, and does not count toward pickup — directly contrary to CD's standard that Group should keep commission and pickup credit on any rate adjustment.
findings.cd_standard: If the hotel sells below the contracted rate, the group's rate should be adjusted (including retroactively) or all such rooms should count toward the block, and Group should keep commission and pickup credit regardless.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel guarantees it will not sell guestrooms at a rate lower than Group's contracted group rate during the Event dates, except for qualified rates (government, airline, contracted corporate rates). If Hotel offers a lower rate, Hotel will adjust the rate for all prior reservations in Group's block to match, and such rooms will remain fully commissionable and creditable toward Group's pickup and complimentary room calculations.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel retains the absolute right to sell rooms to the general public at any rate, including rates below the rate offered to Group.

findings.finding_text: Group waives any right to dispute invoices, finance charges of 1.5%/month compound exceed CD's 1% cap, and prepayment amounts (in lieu of credit approval) are left entirely to Hotel's discretion rather than a defined staged schedule.
findings.cd_standard: Finance charges should be capped at 1% per month or the legal maximum, with a real dispute window before charges apply; if credit is denied, Group should pay on a defined staged deposit schedule (e.g., 25%/25%/50%), not an open-ended prepayment.
findings.proposed_language: Group will have thirty (30) days from receipt of the final itemized invoice to dispute any charge in good faith before any finance charge accrues. A finance charge not to exceed one percent (1.0%) per month, or the maximum allowed by law, whichever is less, will apply only to unpaid, undisputed balances. If credit is denied, Group will pay twenty-five percent (25%) of estimated charges within fourteen (14) business days of denial, twenty-five percent (25%) one month prior to the Event, and fifty percent (50%) three days before the Event.
findings.quoted_text: Where the Hotel has not approved credit for the Group, the Hotel may require prepayment in such amount as the Hotel determines to be appropriate before rooms are held, facilities are reserved, or services are rendered.

findings.finding_text: The $25,000 security deposit may be applied to attrition, F&B shortfalls, cancellation penalties and other unrelated financial obligations rather than being limited to actual property damage, and is refunded within 90 days rather than 30.
findings.cd_standard: Security/damage deposits should be refunded within 30 days absent documented, itemized damage, and should not be commingled with or used to offset attrition or F&B minimum shortfalls.
findings.proposed_language: The security deposit will be refunded in full within thirty (30) days of the event's conclusion unless Hotel provides an itemized accounting of specific, documented property damage caused by Group or its attendees beyond normal wear and tear. The deposit may not be applied toward attrition, cancellation, or F&B minimum shortfalls.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel may apply the security deposit, or such portion thereof as necessary, against any attrition charges, food and beverage shortfalls, damages to the Hotel's premises, incidental costs, outstanding room charges, service failures, cancellation penalties, or any other sum that the Group owes to the Hotel under this Agreement
findings.exposure_basis: Full security deposit amount subject to broad application and delayed refund.

findings.finding_text: Walked guests bear all costs of alternative lodging and transportation themselves, receive no upgrade or amenity upon return, and relocated nights are excluded from Group's pickup/commission — the opposite of CD's standard, and there is no compensation trigger for high-volume walks.
findings.cd_standard: Walked guests should receive comparable-or-better accommodations, round-trip transportation, and a welcome amenity/upgrade on return at Hotel's expense; Group should receive a per-room-night rebate and pickup/commission credit for relocated nights, with additional compensation for walks of 10+ guests or 10%+ of peak night block.
findings.proposed_language: If Hotel is unable to accommodate a guaranteed reservation, Hotel will, at its own expense, provide comparable or better accommodations, round-trip transportation, and message forwarding for the displaced guest, and upon return, an upgrade if available and a welcome amenity. Hotel will credit Group's master account for each night a guest is relocated, and each such night will count toward Group's pickup and commission. If Hotel walks ten (10) or more guests or ten percent (10%) of the peak-night block, Hotel will owe Group additional compensation.
findings.quoted_text: In the event the Hotel is unable to provide accommodations to any guest for whom a reservation has been guaranteed under this Agreement, the Hotel shall make a reasonable effort to secure alternative lodging at the guest's sole expense and cost.

findings.finding_text: The Hotel disclaims any obligation to disclose planned construction/renovation, reserves the right to conduct work without notice or restriction, and Group has no right to terminate, claim damages, or receive a rate reduction even if the work materially disrupts the event.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should represent no current renovation plans affecting the group's space, give 30 days' notice with scope/schedule/mitigation plan for any confirmed work, and allow Group to terminate without liability if the work will interfere with its event.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel represents it has no current plans for renovation affecting the space Group will use, other than ordinary maintenance. If Hotel later confirms such plans, it will notify Group in writing within thirty (30) days, describing scope, schedule, anticipated impact, and mitigation plan. If Group determines the work will interfere with its meeting, Group may terminate this Agreement without liability upon written notice within thirty (30) days of receiving Hotel's notice.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel reserves the right to commence, continue, or complete any construction, renovation, or maintenance work at any time without providing the Group with advance written notice, and without restriction as to timing, scope, noise level, dust, disruption to guest services, or impact on guest experience.

findings.finding_text: Notice of brand/management/ownership change is only 'commercially reasonable efforts' rather than a firm 30-day requirement, Group's termination window is only 10 days rather than 30, and bankruptcy/foreclosure/receivership is expressly excluded from any notice or termination right.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should notify Group within 30 days of a change in brand, management, ownership, bankruptcy, or foreclosure, and Group should be able to terminate without liability within 30 days of that notice.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will inform Group in writing within thirty (30) days of any material change in ownership, management company, or brand affiliation, or of any bankruptcy filing or foreclosure. Group may terminate this Agreement without liability within thirty (30) days of receiving that notice, and Hotel will refund all deposits and prepayments within five (5) days.
findings.quoted_text: the Hotel shall be subject to bankruptcy, foreclosure, receivership, or other insolvency proceedings, and that such events shall not trigger any notice requirement, termination right, or remedy available to the Group.
findings.location_section: 23. Change of Brand, Management or Ownership

findings.finding_text: The Hotel is not obligated to disclose CBA expiration dates or upcoming labor disputes, and Group has no right to cancel for any labor dispute regardless of timing or severity.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should give a year's advance notice of CBA expirations and prompt notice of labor disputes; Group should be able to cancel without liability if a strike, lockout, or expired contract arises within 90 days of the event.
findings.proposed_language: One year in advance, Hotel will provide Group in writing a list of collective bargaining agreement expiration dates for the ensuing year, and will notify Group within ten (10) working days of becoming aware of any labor dispute. If, within ninety (90) days prior to or during the Event, a strike, lockout, or expired labor contract occurs, Group may cancel this Agreement without liability, and any deposits will be promptly refunded.
findings.quoted_text: In the event of a labor dispute, strike, work stoppage, lockout, labor action, or other labor-related event affecting the Hotel or its operations, no cancellation window or notice period is defined herein, and the Group shall have no right to cancel this Agreement based upon the occurrence or threatened occurrence of any such labor-related event.

findings.finding_text: Group is required to use only Hotel-appointed vendors for all services (decorating, AV, florist, photography, etc.) and faces a $2,500 surcharge per unauthorized outside vendor engagement.
findings.cd_standard: Group should be free to use outside vendors of its choice for services like AV, decorating, security, floral, and transportation, at no additional fee or surcharge.
findings.proposed_language: Group reserves the right to utilize the supplier of its choice, at no additional service fee or surcharge, for services or rentals including but not limited to audio-visual, exhibit decorating, security, floral, transportation, and tours. Hotel's in-house vendors are not mandatory for any service category.
findings.quoted_text: Group shall engage for all services at the Hotel only vendors appointed exclusively by the Hotel or operating as part of the Hotel's in-house service divisions, and Group shall not retain, contract with, or permit on the Hotel's premises any outside vendor, supplier, decorator, caterer, audiovisual provider, florist, musician, photographer, or other service provider without the Hotel's prior written consent.
findings.exposure_basis: Stated surcharge of $2,500 per unauthorized outside vendor engagement.

findings.finding_text: Indemnification runs one-way from Group to Hotel, extends to claims arising from the Hotel's own negligence (only gross negligence/willful misconduct excluded), and the Hotel expressly disclaims any reciprocal indemnification obligation to Group.
findings.cd_standard: Indemnification should be mutual, limited to each party's own negligence or willful misconduct, and the group should never indemnify the hotel for the hotel's own negligence.
findings.proposed_language: To the extent permitted by law, each party will indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the other party against claims arising out of the negligence or willful misconduct of the indemnifying party, its employees, agents, or contractors. Neither party indemnifies the other for that other party's own negligence. This provision survives the termination or expiration of this Agreement.
findings.quoted_text: This indemnification obligation shall extend to claims arising from the Hotel's own negligence in its provision of services or maintenance of premises, provided that Group's indemnity shall not extend to claims arising solely from the Hotel's gross negligence or willful misconduct.

findings.finding_text: The Hotel disclaims any warranty of ADA compliance and places the entire burden of funding auxiliary aids on Group regardless of where in the hotel they are needed, with no reciprocal responsibility for the Hotel's own common areas and guest rooms.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should warrant ADA compliance for guest rooms, common areas, function space, and transportation, with each party funding auxiliary aids for its own areas of responsibility (Group for function space, Hotel for guest rooms/common areas).
findings.proposed_language: Hotel warrants that its guest rooms, common areas, function space, and transportation services comply with the public accommodation requirements of the ADA. Group is responsible for funding auxiliary aids needed in the function space held for its use; Hotel is responsible for funding auxiliary aids required by law in guest rooms, public space, and common areas.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel makes no representation, warranty, or covenant regarding the accessibility of its facilities under the Americans with Disabilities Act, as amended, or any state or local accessibility law, and Group assumes sole responsibility for assessing the suitability of the Hotel's premises

findings.finding_text: The Hotel commits to nothing beyond bare legal compliance and Group has no right to terminate if state or local law changes to permit discrimination against attendees.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should commit to nondiscrimination on enumerated grounds even beyond what law requires, and Group should be able to terminate without liability if state/local law changes to permit discrimination.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel agrees that Hotel and its employees and agents will not discriminate against any of Group's attendees on the basis of sex, gender identity or expression, age, race, color, religion, national or ethnic origin, disability, sexual orientation, genetic information, or family, marital, or military status, notwithstanding that such discrimination may be allowed under state or federal law. Should the state or city adopt legislation permitting such discrimination, Group may terminate this Agreement without liability.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel's obligations with respect to nondiscrimination, equal treatment, and protected-class accommodations shall be limited to compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local civil rights laws and public accommodations statutes in effect at the time of the Event.

findings.finding_text: Attendee data may be used by the Hotel for its own marketing and shared with affiliates and third-party marketers without Group's consent, contrary to CD's standard restricting such use.
findings.cd_standard: Rooming list and attendee data should be used solely for fulfilling reservations, not for the hotel's own marketing or third-party disclosure, without the group's consent.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will use rooming list and attendee data solely for the purpose of fulfilling reservations under this Agreement. Hotel will not use such data for its own marketing purposes, nor disclose it to any third party, without Group's prior written consent.
findings.quoted_text: Group acknowledges that the Hotel may utilize such attendee data for the Hotel's own marketing, promotional, and business development purposes, including but not limited to direct mail, email marketing, targeted advertising, and future event solicitation directed to attendees or their affiliated organizations.

findings.finding_text: There is no periodic room block review at 24/12 months, no weekly pickup reports (reports provided only on Group's request at Hotel's convenience), no defined final pickup report within 10 days of departure, the post-event report window is 90 days rather than 30, and there is an explicit waiver of any room-block audit right.
findings.cd_standard: Room block should be reviewed at 24/12 months; Group should get weekly pickup reports, final reports within 10 days of departure, a full post-event report within 30 days, and a no-cost audit right comparing hotel and Group registration lists.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will provide Group a weekly guestroom pickup report starting a set number of days before the cutoff date, final pickup reports within ten (10) days of departure, and a full post-event report within thirty (30) days of departure. At Group's request and at no cost, Hotel will compare its in-house guest list against Group's registration list, and Group will retain the right to audit these records.
findings.quoted_text: Group shall have no right to audit, inspect, or verify the Hotel's room block records, reservation systems, or internal accounting related to Group's event, and Group waives any audit rights it might otherwise possess under applicable law or contract principles.

findings.finding_text: The contract gives the Hotel absolute, unreasoned discretion to withhold consent to any assignment, including to a successor association management company, with no carve-out for affiliated entities or unreasonable-withholding standard.
findings.cd_standard: Group should be able to assign the contract to a successor management company or affiliated entity without the hotel's consent being unreasonably withheld, particularly where the event itself is unchanged.
findings.proposed_language: Group may assign this Agreement to a successor association management company or affiliated entity without Hotel's consent, provided the assignee assumes all obligations under this Agreement and the event dates, room block, and program remain substantially unchanged. Any other assignment requires Hotel's consent, not to be unreasonably withheld.
findings.quoted_text: Hotel's consent to any proposed assignment is entirely within Hotel's sole discretion and may be withheld in Hotel's absolute discretion for any reason whatsoever, or for no reason at all.

findings.finding_text: Governing law and venue are fixed to the Hotel's state (Maryland) rather than Group's location, the Hotel may recover punitive damages, and the prevailing party (deemed to be the Hotel if it recovers any material relief) recovers attorney's fees — the opposite of CD's mutual fee-bearing, no-punitive-damages standard.
findings.cd_standard: Governing law and venue should be the state and city where Group is located, with no punitive damages and each party bearing its own attorney's fees.
findings.proposed_language: This Agreement will be construed in accordance with the laws of the state in which Group is located, and any dispute will be resolved in a court of law in the city in which Group is located. Any award will be limited to actual damages; punitive damages will not be awarded. Each party will be responsible for its own attorney's fees and expenses.
findings.quoted_text: the Hotel shall be entitled to recover, in addition to all other remedies available at law or in equity and in addition to any actual damages awarded, an award of punitive damages to the extent permitted by applicable law.

findings.finding_text: The contract contains no commission clause at all providing for payment of a 10% commission to ConferenceDirect on actualized room revenue.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should pay ConferenceDirect 10% commission on all actualized room revenue, including rooms outside the block, miscoded rooms, walked rooms, and no-show/cancellation-fee room nights, within 30 days of departure, non-cancelable and non-transferable.
findings.proposed_language: All rates confirmed in this Agreement are commissionable at ten percent (10%) to ConferenceDirect, LLC. Hotel will pay commission on all actualized room revenue, regardless of rate paid and including all rooms outside the block, within thirty (30) days of Group's departure, whether or not the master account has been paid in full. Commission is non-cancelable and non-transferable.

findings.finding_text: Rates are already fixed for this single-year event, but the contract contains no cap on future rate increases or provision to lower the rate if market rates decline, which is relevant given the Exhibit A tentative space and potential rebooking.
findings.cd_standard: Where future-year rates are unconfirmed, increases should be capped at 2% per year and the rate should decrease if market/published rates decline, fixed no later than 12 months before the event.
findings.proposed_language: Should any room rates in this Agreement remain unconfirmed for a future contract year, Hotel guarantees a maximum yearly increase of two percent (2%) over quoted rates, and the group rate will be reduced proportionally if market average rates for comparable hotels decline before arrival. Final rates will be confirmed in writing no later than twelve (12) months prior to arrival.

findings.finding_text: The contract does not address what happens if the Hotel closes or materially limits restaurants, spa, fitness facilities, or contracted meeting space, or reduces staffing ratios, leaving Group without recourse for such reductions.
findings.cd_standard: If the hotel closes or limits facilities/services materially, it should first offer equal alternatives at its own expense; if no resolution within 30 days, Group should be able to cancel without liability or renegotiate.
findings.proposed_language: If Hotel closes or limits the hours or capacity of any restaurant, health club, spa, fitness facility, contracted meeting space, or other venue by more than twenty-five percent (25%) of its published capacity, or materially reduces staffing ratios for housekeeping, food service, banquet, engineering, or security services, Hotel will first offer equal alternative facilities or services at its own expense. Should no mutually agreeable alternative be reached within thirty (30) days, Group may cancel this Agreement without liability or the parties may renegotiate terms.

analysis.document_notes: This contract is unusually one-sided across nearly every clause category, systematically stripping Group of audit rights, mitigation protections, and termination remedies while expanding Hotel discretion (e.g., attrition records "final and binding" and unauditable, resale/mitigation duties disclaimed outright, force majeure narrowed to exclude pandemics/government restrictions, and termination-for-cause folded into the cancellation liquidated-damages scale). Several clauses CD's standards call for are entirely absent (commission to ConferenceDirect, future rate cap, facilities/services reduction protection). The function space in Exhibit A is described as "tentative" pending signature and is not firmly assigned or protected from reassignment. Numerous dollar exposure figures could not be precisely calculated due to ambiguity in how nightly block figures interact with resort fees and complimentary room ratios; those were left null or flagged as illustrative only where the underlying contract math was reasonably clear.

findings.finding_text: Attrition liability triggers at 75% pickup rather than the 70% threshold CD's standard requires, meaning Group becomes liable for damages sooner (a smaller pickup shortfall exposes Group to payment). Additionally, the contract's liquidated-damages table in the Cancellation section conflicts with the 70%-lost-profit formula stated in Section 2 attrition language -- damages are calculated at 70% of room rate for unoccupied rooms which appears consistent, but the trigger threshold itself (75% rather than 70%) is a deviation.
findings.cd_standard: Attrition liability should be triggered only if pickup falls below 70% of the block, with damages calculated as 70% lost profit on the single net group rate for rooms the hotel actually failed to sell.
findings.proposed_language: Should Group fail to occupy at least seventy percent (70%) of committed rooms, Group shall pay Hotel liquidated damages equal to seventy percent (70%) of the single net group rate applicable to the unoccupied rooms below that threshold, for each night the threshold is not met, calculated as the lesser of the number of unsold rooms in the Hotel that night or the shortfall between Group's minimum block and actual pickup.
findings.quoted_text: Should Group fail to occupy at least seventy-five percent (75%) of committed rooms, Group shall pay the Hotel liquidated damages equal to the room rate applicable to the unoccupied rooms, multiplied by seventy percent (70%), for each night the threshold is not met.

findings.finding_text: The attrition clause lacks a rebooking credit provision: damages paid should be credited back if a ConferenceDirect client later rebooks the Hotel. The cancellation clause (Section 5) includes a rebooking credit but the attrition clause does not extend this benefit for attrition damages, nor does it provide for F&B minimum overage to offset attrition damages (dollar-for-dollar cross-credit).
findings.cd_standard: Damages paid should be credited back if a ConferenceDirect client later rebooks the hotel, and excess F&B revenue above the minimum should be credited dollar for dollar against room attrition damages, and vice versa.
findings.proposed_language: Should a ConferenceDirect client rebook the Hotel for another meeting within two (2) years, Hotel will credit up to 100% of the attrition damages paid toward the new booking's room revenue, not to exceed the damages paid; if the rebooking group is not the group that paid, the credit will be refunded directly to the group that paid. Any excess food and beverage revenue above Group's F&B minimum will be credited dollar for dollar against room attrition damages, and vice versa.

findings.finding_text: The F&B minimum shortfall is billed at the full dollar-for-dollar shortfall plus an additional 35% penalty on top of the base shortfall, rather than the 35% of shortfall standard CD's contract calls for. This is a substantially harsher formula than CD's position (which caps exposure at 35% of the gap, not 135% of the gap).
findings.cd_standard: Any shortfall should be billed at 35% of the shortfall amount, not the full dollar-for-dollar difference (let alone the full difference plus an additional surcharge).
findings.proposed_language: If Group's actual food and beverage revenue is less than the minimum, Group will pay Hotel thirty-five percent (35%) of the difference between actual revenue and the minimum, not the full shortfall amount and not any additional surcharge above that.
findings.quoted_text: If the Group's actual food and beverage charges fall short of the minimum, the Group shall pay the Hotel the shortfall amount within thirty (30) days of the Hotel's invoice. The Hotel shall calculate the shortfall based on its standard accounting records. Any dispute regarding the calculation must be raised in writing within fourteen (14) days of the invoice; absent a timely dispute, the calculation is deemed accepted. The shortfall rate shall apply to any shortfall amount, assessed at thirty-five percent (35%) in addition to the base shortfall.
findings.exposure_basis: Full F&B minimum of $40,000 is exposed to a dollar-for-dollar shortfall payment plus a 35% surcharge on that shortfall, versus CD's standard of paying only 35% of the shortfall.

findings.finding_text: The F&B minimum clause does not state that revenue from affiliate organizations and exhibitors meeting in conjunction with Group's event will count toward the minimum.
findings.cd_standard: Food and beverage revenue from affiliate organizations and exhibitors should count toward the minimum.
findings.proposed_language: Food and beverage revenue from all affiliate organizations and exhibitors meeting in conjunction with Group's event will count toward the minimum.

findings.finding_text: The liquidated damages table in Section 5 does not match the narrative sliding scale described immediately above it in the same section. The narrative text states damages of 0/25/50/75/100% at tiers of 12+, 9-12, 6-9, 3-6, and under 3 months, while the table below states 0/35/52/63/70% at tiers of 365+, 364-181, 180-91, 90-31, and 30-or-fewer days. This internal contradiction creates ambiguity as to which schedule governs and needs to be resolved; as currently written the table's peak tier (70%) is consistent with CD's 70% cap, but the narrative's escalation to 100% at the closest tier exceeds CD's standard of damages capped at 70% of lost room profit.
findings.cd_standard: Cancellation damages should be a percentage of room profit on a disclosed sliding scale, calculated against 70% of the single net group rate (100% of "room profit") — not escalating beyond that ceiling.
findings.proposed_language: Damages are assessed on a sliding scale based on the date notice is received, calculated as a percentage of room profit (where 100% of room profit equals seventy percent (70%) of the confirmed single net group rate multiplied by the final adjusted room block less allowable attrition), as follows: 365 days or more prior to arrival - none; 364-181 days - 35%; 180-91 days - 52%; 90-31 days - 63%; 30 days or fewer - 70%. This table supersedes and replaces the narrative percentages stated above it in this section.
findings.quoted_text: if notice is given fewer than three (3) months before June 2, 2027, damages equal one hundred (100) percent of lost room profit.

findings.finding_text: The cutoff date is set at 35 days prior to arrival, later than the 21-day maximum CD's standard permits (a cutoff further from arrival reduces the window during which attendees can book at the group rate). Additionally, rooms unassigned at cutoff may be released and sold at the Hotel's sole discretion at any rate without consultation with Group, rather than being held on prepayment or released only after consultation to reduce attrition exposure.
findings.cd_standard: The cutoff date should be no earlier than 21 days prior to arrival, and unassigned rooms at cutoff should either be held for Group on prepayment, refunded if attendees later pay, or released for resale only after consultation with Group to reduce Group's attrition exposure.
findings.proposed_language: The cutoff date for the room block will be twenty-one (21) days prior to Group's major arrival date. After the cutoff date, Hotel will continue to hold any rooms in Group's block not assigned to a specific attendee if Group pays for them in full at that time, refunding those advance payments after the Event for rooms later paid for by attendees; alternatively, after consultation with Group, Hotel will offer unassigned rooms to other individuals or groups to reduce any damages Group may owe under the attrition clause.
findings.quoted_text: All reservations for rooms within the group block must be made on or before thirty-five (35) days prior to arrival. This cutoff date is firm and applies to all reservations made through the Hotel's group reservation desk or online portal.

findings.finding_text: After cutoff, reservations remain at the group rate only "based on availability at the time of request," a narrower, discretionary standard rather than the requirement that the group rate continue to be honored for as long as the Hotel is selling rooms to the general public (or the same room type once the block sells out).
findings.cd_standard: After cutoff, attendees should still get the group rate for as long as the hotel is selling rooms to the general public, rather than a narrower space-available test controlled by the hotel.
findings.proposed_language: Group members may continue to reserve rooms at the group rate for as long as Hotel is selling rooms to the general public, regardless of room type; once the room block has sold, Hotel will honor the group rate for as long as it is selling the contracted room type to the general public.
findings.quoted_text: Reservations requested after the cutoff date remain eligible for the negotiated group rate based on availability at the time of request, provided that the Hotel is under no obligation to hold inventory after the cutoff has passed.

findings.finding_text: The force majeure clause omits several qualifying causes CD's standard requires be explicitly listed: terrorism/threats of terrorism, government closures/emergency declarations, corporate and educational institution travel restrictions, and civil disturbance. It also does not state that Group retains this right even for conditions known at signing, and does not provide that if Group holds a smaller/reduced meeting instead of canceling, Hotel will waive attrition, F&B minimum, and rental fees and offer the lowest rate offered to others. It also lacks the requirement to refund deposits within a specific short window tied to the notice (it's addressed generally as 30 days, which is acceptable, but the reduced-meeting waiver and known-at-signing protection are missing).
findings.cd_standard: Qualifying force majeure causes should explicitly include terrorism, disease/epidemics, CDC/government travel advisories, government closures and emergency declarations, and government, corporate, and educational travel restrictions. Group should retain this right even for conditions known at signing, and if Group holds a smaller meeting instead of cancelling, Hotel should waive attrition, F&B, and rental fees and offer the lowest rate it offers anyone.
findings.proposed_language: Force majeure events include, without limitation, acts of God; war; curtailment of transportation; strikes; threats or acts of terrorism; disease or epidemic; a CDC advisory or governmental travel advisory; full or partial government closure; declaration of a national, state, or local emergency; prohibition of travel by government employees; corporate or educational institution travel restrictions; civil disturbance; government-imposed travel restrictions and official travel advisories restricting travel to Portland, Oregon; and conditions of public safety, health, or infrastructure rendering travel or gathering unsafe or imprudent. Group's right to invoke this clause is not limited by either party's awareness of the condition at the time this Agreement was signed. If Group elects to hold a reduced-size Event despite such circumstances, Hotel will waive any fees related to the reduced size, including room and food and beverage attrition and function space rental, and will offer Group's attendees any lower room rate offered to other guests over the contracted dates.
findings.quoted_text: Force majeure events include, without limitation, government-imposed travel restrictions and official travel advisories that restrict or discourage travel to Portland, Oregon, epidemics and pandemics affecting public health or travel, and conditions of public safety, health, or infrastructure that render it unsafe or imprudent for Group's attendees to travel to or gather at the Hotel or in Portland.

findings.finding_text: The named storm clause requires Group to provide written notice within twelve (12) hours of an NWS warning issuance, a very short and operationally burdensome notice window that is not reflected in CD's fallback (which contemplates a 72-hour forecast trigger with no comparably tight countervailing notice deadline on Group). This tight requirement risks Group losing its cancellation right through administrative delay.
findings.cd_standard: Named storm clauses should give the group a workable notice period tied to the storm's forecast proximity to the event, without imposing an unreasonably short countervailing deadline on the group to provide its own notice.
findings.proposed_language: Group must provide written notice of cancellation to the Hotel's Director of Sales within seventy-two (72) hours of the National Weather Service's issuance of a hurricane or tropical storm warning for the Portland area, or as soon as reasonably practicable thereafter.
findings.quoted_text: Group must provide written notice of cancellation to the Hotel's Director of Sales within twelve (12) hours of the National Weather Service's issuance of a hurricane or tropical storm warning for the Portland area.

findings.finding_text: The gratuity percentage itself is not stated/confirmed anywhere in the contract — only the 22% service charge is quantified. CD's standard calls for both percentages to be confirmed in the contract.
findings.cd_standard: Both the gratuity percentage and the service charge percentage should be confirmed in the contract.
findings.proposed_language: Group shall pay a gratuity of [X]% of the food and beverage subtotal, plus applicable tax, fully distributed to the servers, bussers, and bartenders assigned to the Event, in addition to the service charge of twenty-two percent (22%) described in this section.
findings.quoted_text: Gratuity paid by Group shall be distributed in full to the service staff who worked the event.

findings.finding_text: The staffing ratios stated (one server per 20 guests for all meal types, one bartender per 75 for all bar types) do not match CD's differentiated standard, which calls for more favorable ratios at plated breakfasts (1:25) and buffets (1:40 breakfast, 1:30 lunch/dinner), and a looser cash-bar bartender ratio (1:100). Because this contract uses a flat 1:20 ratio for all meals and flat 1:75 for all bars, it is actually more generous than CD's standard in some respects (e.g., 1:20 vs 1:25 for breakfast) but does not address buffet-specific ratios at all, leaving ambiguity for buffet functions.
findings.cd_standard: Minimum staffing should be one server per 25 at plated breakfast, one per 20 at plated lunch/dinner, one per 40 at buffet breakfast, one per 30 at buffet lunch/dinner, one bartender per 75 at hosted bars, and one bartender per 100 at cash bars.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will provide at least one server for every twenty-five (25) guests at a plated breakfast and every twenty (20) guests at a plated lunch or dinner, and one server for every forty (40) guests at a buffet breakfast and every thirty (30) guests at a buffet lunch or dinner. Hotel will provide no fewer than one (1) bartender for every seventy-five (75) guests at hosted bars and one (1) bartender for every one hundred (100) guests at cash bars.
findings.quoted_text: the Hotel shall maintain minimum staffing ratios as follows: one (1) server for every twenty (20) guests and one (1) bartender for every seventy-five (75) guests.

findings.finding_text: The cost of auxiliary aids in event space is split between Group and Hotel rather than being Group's sole funding responsibility (with Hotel funding aids in guest rooms/common areas), and the clause lacks mutual indemnification limited to each party's own ADA obligations.
findings.cd_standard: Group should fund auxiliary aids needed in the function space held for its use; Hotel should fund auxiliary aids required in guest rooms, public space, and common areas. Each party should indemnify the other only for its own ADA obligations.
findings.proposed_language: Group is responsible for obtaining and funding any auxiliary aids needed in the function space held for its use; Hotel is responsible for obtaining and funding any auxiliary aids required by law in guest rooms, public space, and common areas. Both parties will communicate known auxiliary-aid and accessible-guest-room needs to the other in advance. Hotel and Group will each indemnify and hold harmless the other from liability arising from that party's own obligations under the ADA.
findings.quoted_text: The cost of any auxiliary aids or services requested by Group or its attendees, including but not limited to interpreters, transcription services, specialized audio equipment and accessible transportation, shall be divided between Group and the Hotel.

findings.finding_text: The room block review adjustment allowance is capped at 15% per review date, which is not itself inherently a deviation (CD's standard leaves the percentage as a variable [X]%), but the review dates (July 1, 2026, October 1, 2026, February 1, 2027) do not align to the standard 24-month/12-month-out cadence relative to the June 2, 2027 event -- July 1, 2026 is roughly 23 months out (acceptable) but October 1, 2026 (~20 months) and February 1, 2027 (~16 months) do not correspond to the 24-month/12-month review structure CD calls for, and there is no review closer to 12 months out.
findings.cd_standard: The room block should be reviewed in writing at approximately 24 and 12 months prior to arrival.
findings.proposed_language: The parties acknowledge that the room block shall be subject to written review at the following dates: June 2, 2025 (24 months prior to arrival) and June 2, 2026 (12 months prior to arrival), at which review dates Group may increase or decrease the block by up to [X]% at each review and [X]% cumulatively, at the group rate.
findings.quoted_text: the room block shall be subject to written review at the following dates: July 1, 2026, October 1, 2026, and February 1, 2027, and at each such review date the Group may increase or decrease the block by no more than fifteen percent (15%) of the then-current commitment.

findings.finding_text: There is no stated timeline for delivery of the weekly pickup report relative to the cutoff date (e.g., starting a set number of days before cutoff), and no mention that miscoded rooms at brand-associate or business rates should be credited to Group's pickup regardless of rate paid or reservation method.
findings.cd_standard: Group should get a weekly pickup report starting a set number of days before cutoff, and any miscoded room — including those at brand-associate or business rates or booked through internet distribution channels — should be credited to Group's pickup regardless of the rate paid.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will provide Group a weekly guestroom pickup report starting sixty (60) days prior to the cutoff date. Any guest room occupied by an individual on Group's registration list but not coded to Group within Hotel's system — including rooms booked at qualified brand-associate or business rates or through Internet distribution channels — will be credited to Group's pickup regardless of the rate paid or reservation method.

findings.finding_text: The walk/relocation clause lacks any additional compensation trigger if the Hotel walks 10 or more guests, or 10% or more of the contracted peak-night block, as CD's standard requires.
findings.cd_standard: If the hotel walks 10 or more guests, or 10% or more of the peak-night block, the hotel should owe additional compensation.
findings.proposed_language: If Hotel walks ten (10) or more guests, or ten percent (10%) or more of the contracted peak-night block, Hotel will owe Group reasonable additional compensation.

findings.finding_text: Governing law and venue are tied to the state where Group maintains its principal offices, and punitive damages are excluded with each party bearing its own attorney's fees, all consistent with the position — however this is included here as a document note rather than deviation since it appears to meet the standard.
findings.cd_standard: Governing law and dispute venue should be the state and city where the group is located, with no punitive damages and each party bearing its own attorney's fees.
findings.proposed_language: No change required.

analysis.document_notes: The contract contains an internal inconsistency in Section 5 (Cancellation and Liquidated Damages): the narrative text describes a sliding scale of 0/25/50/75/100% tied to 12/9/6/3-month tiers, while the table immediately below it describes a different scale of 0/35/52/63/70% tied to 365/181/91/30-day tiers. These two schedules do not reconcile and should be clarified with the property as to which governs, as this creates real ambiguity in calculating cancellation exposure. Aside from this, the document is a clean, readable, single-event contract with numbered sections and one attached exhibit (Exhibit A, function space) not included in the text provided for review. The governing_law_venue clause was flagged as a note only to record that it was reviewed and found to align with CD's standard structurally, not as a deviation requiring action -- this is included for completeness of the audit trail given the unusual internal contradiction found elsewhere in the document; going forward treat clauses meeting CD's standard as reflected only in clauses_checked, not as findings entries."

findings.finding_text: Attrition is measured night-by-night rather than cumulatively across the block, liability triggers at any shortfall below 90% (not only below a 70% cumulative threshold), and damages are billed at 90% of the nightly group rate on unoccupied rooms (full gross rate proxy) rather than 70% of lost profit on the net group rate for actually-failed-to-sell rooms. There is also no audit-driven formula requirement beyond documentation, no F&B/attrition cross-credit, and no rebate of damages if a CD client rebooks the hotel.
findings.cd_standard: Attrition liability, if any, will be calculated on a cumulative (not night-by-night) basis, with liability triggered only if Group's actual pickup falls below seventy percent (70%) of the total contracted room block, and damages equal to 70% lost profit on the net group rate, credited back if a CD client rebooks.
findings.proposed_language: Attrition liability, if any, will be calculated on a cumulative (not night-by-night) basis for the entire room block, with liability triggered only if Group's actual pickup falls below seventy percent (70%) of the total contracted room block of 95 rooms. For each unsold room night below that threshold, Group will pay an amount equal to seventy percent (70%) of Group's single confirmed net group rate of $168.00 (plus tax, if required by applicable law). For any night the Hotel achieves 95% occupancy or higher, Group will receive full credit toward its block commitment for that night. Any excess food and beverage revenue above Group's F&B minimum will be credited dollar for dollar against room attrition damages, and vice versa. Should a ConferenceDirect client rebook the Hotel for another meeting within two (2) years, Hotel will credit up to 100% of the attrition damages paid toward the new booking's room revenue.
findings.quoted_text: Attrition is measured on a night-by-night basis, and the Group's block commitment is deemed satisfied only to the extent that occupied rooms meet or exceed ninety percent (90%) of the rooms reserved for each night of the Event.
findings.exposure_basis: 95 rooms x $168/night x 100% shortfall at 90% attrition-rate charge vs. CD's 70%-of-lost-profit standard; illustrative worst-case exposure on peak night block if fully unoccupied: 95 x $168 x 0.90 = $14,364, compounded by night-by-night (rather than cumulative) measurement across a 3-night event.

findings.finding_text: Liquidated damages are calculated against gross room revenue rather than 70% lost room profit on the net group rate, and the hotel has no obligation to mitigate by reselling cancelled rooms and crediting proceeds — the contract explicitly states resold-room revenue is retained by the Hotel with no credit applied. There is also no rebate of damages paid if a CD client later rebooks.
findings.cd_standard: Liquidated damages should be calculated as a percentage of room profit (70% of net group rate) on a sliding scale, with hotel obligated to mitigate by reselling and crediting proceeds, and a rebooking credit if a CD client rebooks.
findings.proposed_language: Liquidated damages will be calculated as a percentage of room profit, defined as seventy percent (70%) of the confirmed single net group rate of $168.00 at the time of cancellation, multiplied by the final adjusted room block less allowable attrition, using the sliding scale set forth in this Agreement. Hotel will undertake all reasonable efforts to resell cancelled rooms and food and beverage functions, and will credit those revenues against the cancellation damages, not to exceed the full amount of such damages. Should a ConferenceDirect client rebook the Hotel for another meeting within two (2) years, Hotel will credit up to 100% of the cancellation damages paid toward the new booking's room revenue.
findings.quoted_text: the Group shall owe liquidated damages calculated as a percentage of gross room revenue that would have been earned on the cancelled or reduced rooms, based on the nightly group rates in effect at the time of cancellation
findings.exposure_basis: 95 rooms x $168/night x 70% (highest tier, cancellation within 30 days) using gross revenue basis rather than 70%-of-net-profit basis: 95 x 168 x 0.70 = $11,172 per night baseline; across a 3-night peak commitment the gross-basis calculation materially exceeds the 70%-lost-profit standard.

findings.finding_text: The contract affirmatively denies any mitigation duty: resold-room revenue is retained by the Hotel with no credit against Group's liquidated damages, and there is no requirement to document mitigation efforts or delay damages until 30 days post-event pending evidence of unsold inventory.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should have an affirmative, documented duty to resell canceled rooms/functions and credit proceeds against damages owed, with damages not due until 30 days after the event and only upon evidence of mitigation.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will undertake all reasonable efforts to resell cancelled rooms and food and beverage functions, and will credit those revenues against any cancellation or attrition damages owed by Group, not to exceed the full amount of such damages. Hotel will document in writing its efforts to market the dates proactively through all group and transient channels. Cancellation damages, if any, are due thirty (30) days after the meeting dates, provided Hotel supplies reasonable evidence of its mitigation efforts and that the rooms and space held for Group went unsold.
findings.quoted_text: Any revenue the Hotel generates by reselling rooms within the cancelled portion of the Group's block shall be retained by the Hotel with no credit applied against the Group's liquidated damages obligation.

findings.finding_text: The force majeure clause omits several qualifying causes CD requires (terrorism, war, strikes, civil disturbance, CDC/government travel advisories by name, government closures) and does not include the 20%-attendee-cancellation trigger; it also imposes an unreasonably short 5-business-day notice window tied to when the event/restriction occurs, rather than allowing notice at any time before the event, and does not preserve the right to invoke force majeure even for conditions known at signing. There is also no provision allowing Group to hold a smaller meeting with attrition/F&B/rental fees waived and lowest available rate offered.
findings.cd_standard: Force majeure should allow cancellation for a broad enumerated list of causes including terrorism, disease/epidemic, CDC/government advisories, government closures, and corporate/educational travel restrictions, plus a 20%-attendee-cancellation trigger, with notice permitted any time before the event regardless of awareness at signing, and reduced-meeting fee waivers.
findings.proposed_language: Either party may cancel this Agreement without liability upon written notice to the other party should any cause beyond the control of Hotel or Group — including, but not limited to, acts of God; war; curtailment or interruption of transportation facilities; strikes; threats or acts of terrorism; disease or epidemic; a CDC advisory or governmental travel advisory; full or partial government closure; declaration of emergency; government, corporate, or educational institution travel restrictions; or civil disturbance — in that party's reasonable judgment make performance illegal, impossible, commercially impracticable, or inadvisable, or cause or lead Group to reasonably anticipate that twenty percent (20%) or more of attendees will cancel. Notice may be given at any time before the Event, whether or not the circumstances remain in effect, and Group's right to invoke this clause is not limited by either party's awareness of the condition at signing. If Group elects to hold a reduced-size Event, Hotel will waive attrition, food and beverage minimum, and function space rental fees, and will offer Group's attendees the lowest room rate offered to any other guests over the contracted dates.
findings.quoted_text: The party seeking to invoke force majeure must provide written notice within five (5) business days of the event or restriction, accompanied by reasonable evidence of its occurrence and material impact on performance.

findings.finding_text: The 'Termination for Cause' clause only covers material breach with a cure period; it does not include the broader set of no-liability termination triggers CD requires (Group's own judgment on epidemic/pandemic affecting its ability to hold the meeting, labor disputes, brand/ownership/management change, renovation interference, facility/service reductions, convention center/overflow hotel unavailability, or discriminatory legislation).
findings.cd_standard: Group should be able to terminate without liability for force majeure; Group's own epidemic/pandemic judgment; labor disputes; brand/ownership/management change; renovation interference; facility/service reduction; convention center/overflow hotel unavailability; and discriminatory legislation — separate from the cancellation liquidated-damages scale.
findings.proposed_language: Group may terminate this Agreement without liability, and Hotel will refund all deposits and prepayments within five (5) days, upon any of the following: (a) force majeure as defined in this Agreement; (b) Group's determination that an infectious disease outbreak, epidemic, or pandemic is affecting Group's ability to hold the Event as intended; (c) a labor dispute involving Hotel's employees arising within ninety (90) days of or during the Event; (d) a material change in Hotel's ownership, management company, or brand affiliation, or Hotel's bankruptcy or foreclosure; (e) renovation or remodeling that Group determines will interfere with its meeting; (f) a reduction in Hotel's facilities or services for which no mutually agreeable alternative is reached within thirty (30) days; (g) unavailability of any convention center or overflow hotels on which the Event depends; or (h) adoption of state or local legislation permitting discrimination against attendees. None of the foregoing triggers the liquidated-damages calculation in the cancellation clause.

findings.finding_text: The contract contains no provision addressing a change in the Hotel's brand, ownership, or management, or bankruptcy/foreclosure, and no corresponding right for Group to terminate without liability.
findings.cd_standard: If the hotel changes brand, management, or ownership, or files for bankruptcy/foreclosure, before the event, it should notify Group within 30 days and Group should be able to terminate without liability within 30 days of that notice, with prompt refund.
findings.proposed_language: Should Hotel undergo a material change in ownership, management company, or brand affiliation, or file for bankruptcy, or have foreclosure occur, Hotel will inform Group in writing within thirty (30) days of such change or filing.
