Group may, at its sole discretion, terminate this Agreement without liability within thirty (30) days of receiving that notice. Hotel will refund all deposits and prepayments made by Group within five (5) days of the notice of termination.

findings.finding_text: While the deposit amount is zero and the refund/documentation mechanics otherwise track CD's position, worth noting no issue exists here beyond the deposit amount itself.
findings.cd_standard: Any security or damage deposit should be reasonable, refundable within 30 days absent documented itemized damage, and not commingled with attrition/F&B charges.
findings.proposed_language: No change needed to the deposit amount; confirm the $0.00 security deposit remains in the final executed agreement.
findings.quoted_text: Group shall provide to Hotel a security deposit in the amount of zero dollars, which deposit shall be held by Hotel to secure Group's performance under this Agreement.

findings.finding_text: The finance-charge provision compounds monthly on unpaid balances rather than applying a flat, capped rate; it also lacks a defined dispute window before the finance charge accrues (charges accrue after 30 days regardless of a live dispute) and does not address automatic credit extension if the hotel fails to send a credit application, nor a staged deposit schedule if credit is denied.
findings.cd_standard: Any finance charge on a late, undisputed balance should be capped at 1% per month or the legal maximum, whichever is less (not compounding), with a genuine dispute window before charges accrue; credit should be extended automatically if the hotel never sends a credit application, and a staged deposit schedule should apply if credit is denied.
findings.proposed_language: If payment of all undisputed charges is not received within thirty (30) days of the final invoice, a finance charge not to exceed one percent (1.0%) per month, or the maximum allowed by law, whichever is less, will apply to the unpaid, undisputed balance, and will not compound. Group will have thirty (30) days from receipt of the final itemized invoice to dispute any charge in good faith before any finance charge accrues on the disputed amount. If Hotel fails to send Group a credit application, or fails to send a written reminder to complete it, Hotel will extend credit to Group. If credit is denied, Group will pay twenty-five percent (25%) of estimated charges within fourteen (14) business days of the denial, twenty-five percent (25%) one (1) month prior to the Event, and fifty percent (50%) three (3) days before the Event.
findings.quoted_text: the Hotel shall assess a monthly finance charge of one percent (1%) on the unpaid balance, compounding monthly until paid in full

findings.finding_text: The contract has no provision requiring the Hotel to disclose collective bargaining agreement expiration dates a year in advance, no prompt notice requirement for actual labor disputes, and no right for Group to cancel without liability if a strike, lockout, or expired union contract arises within 90 days of the event.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should give a year's advance notice of CBA expirations and prompt notice of labor disputes; Group should be able to cancel with no liability if a strike/lockout/expired contract arises within 90 days of the event.
findings.proposed_language: One year in advance, or no later than [date], Hotel will provide Group in writing a list of all collective bargaining agreement expiration dates for the ensuing year. Hotel will notify Group in writing within ten (10) working days after becoming aware of any labor dispute involving Hotel's employees. If, within ninety (90) days prior to or during the Event, Hotel's contract with its union employees has expired, picketing occurs, or a strike or lockout occurs, Group may cancel this Agreement by written notice without liability, regardless of whether Hotel is able to perform.

findings.finding_text: The contract contains no provision defining or disclosing gratuity or service charge percentages for food and beverage functions, leaving the treatment of any such charges entirely undefined.
findings.cd_standard: Gratuity and service charge should be clearly and separately defined and disclosed, with both percentages confirmed in the contract, gratuity fully distributed to staff, and neither added to room rental or equipment already carrying a labor fee.
findings.proposed_language: [X]% of the food and beverage total, plus applicable tax, will be added to Group's account as a gratuity and fully distributed to the servers, bussers, and bartenders assigned to the Event. Any separate service charge of [X]%, plus applicable tax, is not distributed as a tip and is retained by Hotel. Both percentages are confirmed in this Agreement. Hotel will not add a gratuity or service charge to meeting room rental fees or to any rented equipment that also carries a labor fee.

findings.finding_text: San Antonio, Texas is within the Gulf Coast hurricane-exposure region, and the contract lacks any separate named-storm clause addressing notice periods and cancellation rights distinct from the general force majeure provision.
findings.cd_standard: Coastal/hurricane-belt markets should have a separate, narrower named-storm clause with its own notice period and cancellation window.
findings.proposed_language: In the event a named storm (hurricane, tropical storm) is forecast to affect the Hotel's location within 72 hours of any event date, either party may cancel the affected portion of the event without liability upon written or verbal (followed by written) notice, regardless of whether the storm ultimately causes physical damage to the Hotel.

findings.finding_text: The contract contains no restriction on the Hotel's use of rooming list or attendee data for its own marketing purposes or disclosure to third parties.
findings.cd_standard: Rooming list and attendee data should not be used by the hotel for its own marketing or sold to third parties without Group's consent.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will use rooming list and attendee data solely for the purpose of fulfilling reservations under this Agreement. Hotel will not use such data for its own marketing purposes, nor disclose it to any third party, without Group's prior written consent.

findings.finding_text: The contract contains no rate-parity guarantee ensuring the Hotel will not sell rooms at a lower rate than Group's contracted rate during the event dates, nor any protection ensuring Group's rate is no higher than any other group's rate within 7 days of the event.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should guarantee it won't sell rooms at a lower rate than the group's contracted rate during the event dates, with remedies if it does, and the rate should be no higher than any other group's rate within 7 days either side of the event.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel guarantees it will not sell guestrooms at a rate lower than Group's contracted group rate of $168.00 during the Event dates, with the exception of qualified rates (government, airline, and contracted corporate negotiated rates). If Hotel offers a lower guestroom rate, Hotel will adjust the rate for all prior reservations in Group's block to match. Hotel further agrees that Group's rate will be no higher than the group rate given to any other group over the period from seven (7) days before through seven (7) days after the room block dates.

findings.finding_text: The contract contains no commission provision at all, leaving ConferenceDirect's 10% commission on actualized room revenue undocumented and unenforceable under this agreement.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should pay ConferenceDirect 10% commission on all actualized room revenue, including rooms outside the block, miscoded rooms, walked rooms, and no-show/cancellation-fee credited nights, within 30 days of departure, non-cancelable and non-transferable.
findings.proposed_language: All rates confirmed in this Agreement are commissionable at ten percent (10%) to ConferenceDirect, LLC. Hotel will pay commission to ConferenceDirect on all actualized room revenue, regardless of rate paid and including all rooms outside the block, within thirty (30) days of Group's departure, whether or not the master account has been paid in full. Commission for this booking is non-cancelable and non-transferable. Hotel will pay ConferenceDirect ten percent (10%) of any liquidated damages paid by Group within ten (10) days of receiving them.

findings.finding_text: The contract contains no provision addressing what happens if the Hotel itself cancels the agreement without a contractual right to do so; there is no obligation for the Hotel to cover Group's resulting direct, indirect, and consequential damages.
findings.cd_standard: If the hotel cancels without a contractual right to do so, it should owe the group all direct, indirect, and consequential damages, not just a deposit refund.
findings.proposed_language: In the event Hotel cancels this Agreement other than as permitted under this Agreement, Hotel will pay Group for all direct, indirect, and consequential damages, expenses, attorney's fees, and costs incurred by Group on account of such cancellation, including but not limited to staff time and travel expenses to secure an alternate location, incremental room rate and airfare differentials, function space rental, and long distance telephone, postage, and printing costs.

findings.finding_text: The contract contains no function space provisions at all — no named function rooms, square footage, ceiling height, room rental waiver, or complimentary meeting-room equipment commitments (microphone, podium, power, lighting, HVAC).
findings.cd_standard: The contract should name each function room with minimum square footage and ceiling height, waive room rental for meeting space in the program agenda, and provide a wired microphone, podium, power, lighting, and HVAC at no charge in each meeting room.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will hold the meeting and function space set out in this Agreement, with room rental charges waived, and will specify each function space assignment, minimum square footage, and ceiling height requirement in this Agreement. No change will be made to the function space assignments without the written consent of both parties. Hotel will provide in each meeting room, at no charge, one wired microphone, a podium, power, proper lighting, and HVAC.

findings.finding_text: The contract has no provision addressing closure or limitation of hotel facilities (restaurants, spa, fitness, meeting space) or reduced staffing ratios, and no corresponding right for Group to cancel or renegotiate if no alternative is reached.
findings.cd_standard: If the hotel closes or limits facilities/services by more than 25% or reduces staffing ratios materially, it should first offer equal alternatives; if no agreement within 30 days, Group should be able to cancel without liability or renegotiate.
findings.proposed_language: If Hotel closes or limits the hours of service of any current restaurant, health club, spa, fitness facility, contracted meeting space, or other hospitality venue by more than twenty-five percent (25%) of its published capacity, or materially reduces guest-to-staff service ratios, Hotel will first offer equal alternative facilities or services at its own expense. Should no mutually agreeable alternative be reached within thirty (30) days, Group may cancel this Agreement without liability, or the parties may modify this Agreement on mutually agreed terms.

findings.finding_text: The contract contains no nondiscrimination commitment for attendees and no corresponding termination right if state or local legislation permits discrimination against attendees.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should commit that it and its staff will not discriminate against attendees on enumerated grounds, and Group should be able to terminate without liability if discriminatory legislation is adopted.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel agrees that Hotel and its employees and agents will not discriminate against any of Group's attendees on the basis of sex, gender identity or expression, age, race, color, religion, national or ethnic origin, disability, sexual orientation, genetic information, or parental, marital, or military status. Should the state of Texas or the city of San Antonio adopt legislation that affirmatively allows such discrimination, Group may terminate this Agreement without liability.

findings.finding_text: The contract contains no reservation-handling provisions covering confirmation timelines, name changes, individual cancellation deadlines, no-show reinstatement, or crediting of individual cancellation money against Group's attrition.
findings.cd_standard: Reservation confirmations, name changes at the group rate, no-charge individual cancellation until 6 pm day of arrival, no-show reinstatement, and crediting individual cancellation money against attrition.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will send each registered guest confirmation of their reservation within four (4) days of receiving the information. Name changes may be made at the group rate up to the arrival date. No cancellation fee will be assessed for any room cancelled before 6:00 p.m. on the day of arrival. Hotel will reinstate no-shows for the following night at the rate of their existing reservation. Any individual cancellation money Hotel receives will be credited toward any attrition damages owed by Group.

findings.finding_text: The contract contains no guaranteed staffing ratios for food and beverage functions (servers, bartenders) and no cap on labor fees for smaller functions.
findings.cd_standard: Minimum staffing ratios for plated/buffet meals and bars should be guaranteed with no labor fee for meeting those ratios, and a labor fee only for functions under 25 people.
findings.proposed_language: At all meal functions, Hotel will provide at least one server for every twenty-five (25) guests at a plated breakfast and every twenty (20) guests at a plated lunch or dinner, and one server for every forty (40) guests at a buffet breakfast and every thirty (30) guests at a buffet lunch or dinner, with no extra service charge. Hotel will provide one bartender for every seventy-five (75) guests at hosted bars and one hundred (100) guests at cash bars, with no bartender fee.

findings.finding_text: The contract contains no audio-visual or internet bandwidth pricing commitment, no minimum bandwidth guarantee, and no discount for add-on AV/internet needs.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should honor attached AV/internet quotes with a minimum of 10 Mbps download/1 Mbps upload, and discount later additions regardless of provider.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will honor the pricing of the attached audio-visual quote and will apply a discount of [X]% to any additional audio-visual needs. Hotel will provide internet bandwidth of a minimum of 10 Mbps download and 1 Mbps upload, with a discount of [X]% on any additional bandwidth needs. Use of Hotel's in-house audio-visual provider will not be a condition of any discounted or complimentary service.

findings.finding_text: The contract contains no ADA compliance warranty or division of responsibility for auxiliary aids between Group (function space) and Hotel (guest rooms/common areas).
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should warrant ADA compliance for guest rooms, common areas, function space, and transportation, with mutual indemnification limited to each party's own ADA obligations and a clear division of auxiliary-aid funding.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel warrants that its guest rooms, common areas, function space, and transportation services comply with the public accommodation requirements of the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA). Group is responsible for obtaining and funding any auxiliary aids needed in the function space held for its use; Hotel is responsible for obtaining and funding any auxiliary aids required by law in guest rooms, public space, and common areas.

findings.finding_text: The contract contains no representation regarding current or planned renovation, no notice obligation for future renovation plans, and no termination right if renovation interferes with Group's event.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should represent no current renovation plans affecting Group's space, commit to 30 days' notice of confirmed later renovation, and allow Group to terminate without liability if the work will interfere with its event.
findings.proposed_language: As of the date of this Agreement, Hotel has no plans for renovation or remodeling of any facilities to be used by Group, other than ordinary maintenance. If Hotel later confirms any such plans, Hotel will notify Group in writing within thirty (30) days, describing the scope, schedule, anticipated impact, and mitigation plan. If Group determines the construction will interfere with its meeting, Group may terminate this Agreement without liability upon written notice given within thirty (30) days of receiving Hotel's plans.

findings.finding_text: The contract contains no provision allowing Group to assign the agreement to a successor management company or affiliated entity without the Hotel's consent being unreasonably withheld.
findings.cd_standard: Group should be able to assign the contract to a successor association management company or affiliated entity without the hotel's consent being unreasonably withheld, where the event itself is unchanged.
findings.proposed_language: Group may assign this Agreement to a successor association management company or affiliated entity without Hotel's consent, provided the assignee assumes all obligations under this Agreement and the event dates, room block, and program remain substantially unchanged. Any other assignment requires Hotel's consent, not to be unreasonably withheld.

findings.finding_text: The contract contains no room-block review dates at 24/12 months, no weekly pickup reports, no defined post-event report contents, and no no-cost room-block audit right against the hotel's in-house guest list.
findings.cd_standard: Room block should be reviewed at 24 and 12 months, with weekly pickup reports, a full post-event report within 30 days, and a no-cost audit right with miscoded rooms credited to Group's pickup.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel and Group will review the room block in writing 24 months and again 12 months prior to arrival. Hotel will provide Group a weekly guestroom pickup report starting thirty (30) days prior to the cutoff date, and a full post-event report within thirty (30) days of departure. At Group's request and at no cost, Hotel will compare its in-house guest list against Group's registration list, and any miscoded room will be credited to Group's pickup regardless of rate paid.

analysis.document_notes: The contract is a fairly short-form agreement lacking many of the operational clauses CD's standards library expects (function space, banquet staffing, AV/internet, ADA, construction/renovation, rate parity, commission, nondiscrimination, labor disputes, review/audit dates, reservation procedures, assignment). These appear to simply be absent from the document rather than addressed elsewhere. No exhibits, riders, or attachments (e.g., AV quote, function space grid) were provided with the text supplied. The walk/relocation clause and future rate cap clause were also entirely absent, but since this is a single-year, already-rated 2027 event with no indication of a multi-year rate structure or overbooking history, these are noted as gaps to raise with the property. Rate figures for the group rate ($168/night) and F&B minimum ($8,500) were the only monetary figures available to calculate exposure against; several exposure amounts could not be quantified given the missing/undefined data (e.g., commission and function space figures) and were left null in accordance with the no-invention rule."

findings.finding_text: Attrition liability triggers at 75% pickup rather than CD's standard 70% threshold, and damages are calculated at 75% of the average daily room rate rather than 70% of the single net group rate. The clause also lacks any dollar-for-dollar F&B/attrition offset provision and lacks a rebate-back for a ConferenceDirect client rebooking.
findings.cd_standard: Liability should trigger only below 70% cumulative pickup, with damages of 70% lost profit on the single net group rate, and should include F&B/attrition crediting and a rebooking credit-back.
findings.proposed_language: Attrition liability, if any, will be triggered only if Group's actual pickup falls below seventy percent (70%) of the total contracted room block, calculated cumulatively. For each unsold room night below that threshold, Group will pay an amount equal to seventy percent (70%) of Group's single confirmed net group rate ($419.00), plus tax if required by law. Any excess food and beverage revenue above Group's F&B minimum will be credited dollar for dollar against room attrition damages, and vice versa. Should a ConferenceDirect client rebook the Hotel within two (2) years, Hotel will credit up to 100% of the attrition damages paid toward the new booking's room revenue.
findings.quoted_text: If Group fails to occupy at least seventy-five percent (75%) of the room block reserved for the Event, Hotel shall assess attrition damages against Group in accordance with the provisions of this clause.

findings.finding_text: Menu pricing is locked 14 months prior to the event, exceeding CD's 12-month maximum, and the shortfall penalty is 40% of the difference rather than CD's 35% standard. The clause also grants the Hotel unilateral discretion to negotiate or waive the shortfall, and does not count affiliate/exhibitor F&B revenue toward the minimum.
findings.cd_standard: Menu pricing should be locked no earlier than 12 months before the event, shortfall should be billed at 35% of the gap, and affiliate/exhibitor F&B revenue should count toward the minimum.
findings.proposed_language: The Hotel shall provide Group with a menu and pricing proposal not earlier than twelve (12) months prior to the Event date, and all menu selections and per-person pricing shall be locked as of that date. If actual food and beverage revenue is less than the Minimum Commitment, Group will pay Hotel thirty-five percent (35%) of the difference between actual revenue and the Minimum, not forty percent (40%). Food and beverage revenue from all affiliate organizations and exhibitors meeting in conjunction with Group's Event will count toward the Minimum.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel shall provide Group with a menu and pricing proposal at least fourteen (14) months prior to the Event date, and all menu selections and per-person pricing shall be locked and shall not be subject to increase or modification after that date.

findings.finding_text: The rooming list/cutoff deadline is set at 32 days prior to arrival, exceeding CD's 21-day maximum, and there is no provision requiring the Hotel to hold unassigned block rooms on prepayment or release them only after consultation with Group to reduce attrition exposure.
findings.cd_standard: The cutoff date should be no earlier than 21 days prior to arrival, and unassigned rooms at cutoff should be held on prepayment, refunded, or released only after consultation with Group.
findings.proposed_language: The cutoff date for the room block will be twenty-one (21) days prior to Group's major arrival date. After the cutoff date, Hotel will continue to hold any unassigned rooms in Group's block if Group pays for them in full, refunding those advance payments for rooms later paid for by attendees; alternatively, after consultation with Group, Hotel will offer unassigned rooms to reduce any attrition damages owed by Group.
findings.quoted_text: Group shall provide the Hotel with a final rooming list containing all guest names, room type preferences, and arrival and departure dates no later than thirty-two (32) days prior to the Event's opening day.

findings.finding_text: Damages are calculated against the average daily room rate rather than the CD standard of 70% of the single net group rate applied to lost room profit, and the liability-free cancellation window is 12 months (matching CD standard) but the sliding scale tiers (35%-70%) are not disclosed as calculated against room profit at CD's specified 70% formula — the contract uses full ADR-based percentages without the 70% lost-profit discount built in.
findings.cd_standard: Cancellation damages should be calculated as a percentage of room profit, defined as 70% of the single net group rate multiplied by the block less allowable attrition, not the full average daily room rate.
findings.proposed_language: Liquidated damages will be calculated as a percentage of room profit, with room profit defined as seventy percent (70%) of the confirmed single net group rate ($419.00) at the time of cancellation, multiplied by the final adjusted room block less allowable attrition, per the sliding scale in Schedule A.
findings.quoted_text: Group shall pay liquidated damages to the Hotel, which the parties acknowledge are not penalties but a reasonable pre-estimate of harm, calculated as a percentage of lost room profit based on the average daily room rate for the negotiated block

findings.finding_text: The force majeure clause does not provide a right to cancel based on Group's reasonable anticipation of 20% or more attendee cancellations, does not address the scenario of Group holding a smaller meeting (with attrition/F&B/rental fee waivers and lowest available rate), and does not clarify that the right survives even if the condition was known at signing.
findings.cd_standard: Force majeure rights should extend to reasonably anticipated 20%+ attendee cancellations, should not be limited by knowledge of the condition at signing, and should provide fee waivers plus lowest available rate if Group holds a smaller meeting instead of canceling.
findings.proposed_language: Either party may cancel this Agreement without liability where a qualifying cause would, in that party's reasonable judgment, cause or lead Group to reasonably anticipate that twenty percent (20%) or more of attendees will cancel. Group's right to invoke this clause is not limited by either party's awareness of the condition when this Agreement was signed. If Group elects to hold the Event at reduced size despite such circumstances, Hotel will waive attrition, food and beverage minimum, and function space rental fees, and will offer Group's attendees the lowest room rate offered to other guests over the contracted dates.
findings.quoted_text: Notwithstanding any other provision of this Agreement, neither party shall be held in breach or default where delays or defaults in performance result from acts or events beyond the reasonable control of that party, including but not limited to circumstances that render performance illegal, impossible or commercially impracticable.

findings.finding_text: The named storm cancellation window is 60 hours prior to the first event date, shorter than CD's standard 72-hour window.
findings.cd_standard: The named storm clause should provide a cancellation window of at least 72 hours before any affected event date.
findings.proposed_language: In the event a named storm is forecast to affect the Hotel's location within seventy-two (72) hours of any event date, either party may cancel the affected portion of the event without liability upon written or verbal (followed by written) notice.
findings.quoted_text: A named storm cancellation window of sixty (60) hours prior to the first event date shall apply

findings.finding_text: The contract only addresses the Hotel's right to terminate for Group's cause; it does not provide Group with a standalone termination right (separate from cancellation liquidated damages) for causes such as a pandemic materially affecting Group's ability to hold the meeting, hotel labor disputes, brand/ownership change, facility reductions, dependence on a convention center/overflow hotel, or discriminatory legislation, tied together as one no-liability termination clause.
findings.cd_standard: Group should have a broad no-liability termination right covering force majeure, pandemic determination, labor disputes, ownership/brand change, facility reductions, convention center/overflow hotel unavailability, and discriminatory legislation, entirely separate from the cancellation liquidated-damages scale.
findings.proposed_language: Group may terminate this Agreement without liability, and Hotel will refund all deposits and prepayments within five (5) days, upon any of the following: (a) force majeure as defined in this Agreement; (b) Group's determination that an infectious disease outbreak, epidemic, or pandemic is affecting Group's ability to hold the Event as intended; (c) a labor dispute involving Hotel's employees arising within ninety (90) days of or during the Event; (d) a material change in Hotel's ownership, management company, or brand affiliation, or Hotel's bankruptcy or foreclosure; (e) renovation interfering with Group's meeting; (f) a reduction in Hotel's facilities or services for which no mutually agreeable alternative is reached within thirty (30) days; (g) unavailability of any convention center or overflow hotels on which the Event depends; or (h) adoption of legislation permitting discrimination against attendees. None of the foregoing will trigger the liquidated-damages calculation in the cancellation clause.

findings.finding_text: Insurance is required of Group only, with no corresponding obligation for the Hotel to carry adequate insurance for its own activities, contrary to CD's mutual-insurance standard.
findings.cd_standard: Insurance should be a mutual obligation, with each party carrying adequate insurance to protect its own activities.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel and Group will each carry adequate insurance to protect their respective activities against claims arising out of the Event. The Group shall obtain and maintain comprehensive general liability insurance with a minimum limit of $2,500,000.00 per occurrence, as set forth above.
findings.quoted_text: The Group shall obtain and maintain comprehensive general liability insurance with a minimum limit of "$2,500,000.00" per occurrence, covering bodily injury, property damage, and contractual liability arising out of the Group's occupancy and use of the Hotel's premises.

findings.finding_text: The auxiliary aid cost allocation is left to case-by-case good-faith negotiation and open-ended cost-splitting, rather than a clear division where Group funds aids in its function space and the Hotel funds aids in guest rooms/common areas as required by law.
findings.cd_standard: There should be a clear division of who funds auxiliary aids in event space (Group) versus guest rooms and common areas (Hotel), rather than a negotiated split.
findings.proposed_language: Group is responsible for obtaining and funding any auxiliary aids needed in the function space held for its use; Hotel is responsible for obtaining and funding any auxiliary aids required by law in guest rooms, public space, and common areas. Both parties will communicate known auxiliary-aid and accessible-guest-room needs to the other in advance.
findings.quoted_text: the cost of such auxiliary aids shall be divided between the Group and the Hotel... the parties shall negotiate in good faith to determine the appropriate allocation of costs for each specific auxiliary aid

findings.finding_text: This clause already ties governing law and venue to Group's home state, which matches CD's standard, so no finding beyond noting the venue is specifically 'exclusive jurisdiction' rather than simply 'a court of law' — this is a marginal wording difference not requiring correction.
findings.cd_standard: Governing law and venue should be the state/city where Group is located, with no punitive damages and each party bearing its own fees.
findings.proposed_language: N/A

findings.finding_text: Advance notice of collective bargaining agreement expirations is required only 9 months out, short of CD's standard of one year's advance notice.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should give a year's advance notice of when its collective bargaining agreements expire.
findings.proposed_language: The Hotel shall provide written notice to the Group of any expiration, non-renewal, or material breach in any collective bargaining agreement covering employees at the Hotel no later than twelve (12) months prior to the expiration date of such agreement.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel shall provide written notice to the Group of any expiration, non-renewal, or material breach in any collective bargaining agreement, union contract, or labor agreement covering employees at the Hotel no later than nine (9) months prior to the expiration date of such agreement.

findings.finding_text: The gratuity and service charge percentages are otherwise clearly disclosed and distinguished (gratuity distributed to staff; 22% service charge retained by the Hotel), meeting the core disclosure standard; however, the gratuity percentage itself is never stated as a numeric figure anywhere in the clause, unlike the service charge.
findings.cd_standard: Both the gratuity percentage and the service charge percentage should be confirmed numerically in the contract.
findings.proposed_language: State the gratuity percentage explicitly: '[X]% of the food and beverage total, plus applicable tax, will be added to Group's account as a gratuity and fully distributed to the staff.' Confirm this percentage in the Agreement alongside the 22% service charge.
findings.quoted_text: All gratuity collected by the Hotel on behalf of Group shall be distributed in full to the staff members who performed services for the Event

findings.finding_text: While resort fees are waived and undisclosed fees are automatically waived (both matching CD's standard), the clause does not address waiving early check-in fees or checked-bag fees for attendees, which CD's standard also calls for.
findings.cd_standard: Attendees should not pay early check-in or checked-bag fees.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will not charge attendees an early check-in fee when their room type is available, and will waive checked-bag fees for attendees arriving before check-in time or departing after check-out time.

findings.finding_text: The complimentary room ratio is set at 1 per 45 paid room nights rather than CD's standard ratio of 1 per 40, and the clause does not address crediting miscoded rooms or no-show/cancellation fee nights toward the complimentary room calculation, nor complimentary in-room internet regardless of loyalty status.
findings.cd_standard: Complimentary rooms should be earned at a ratio of 1 per 40 occupied room nights, counting miscoded rooms and no-show/cancellation fee nights, plus complimentary in-room internet regardless of loyalty status.
findings.proposed_language: Group will receive one (1) complimentary room for every forty (40) occupied, revenue-producing room nights actualized, calculated cumulatively across the entire room block. All occupied rooms will be counted toward Group's pickup, including rooms credited to Group through a room block audit, and each no-show or cancellation fee charged will be credited as one (1) room night toward this calculation. Hotel will provide complimentary internet in attendees' guest rooms regardless of brand loyalty program participation.
findings.quoted_text: The complimentary room ratio is forty-five (45), meaning that for every forty-five (45) paid room nights generated by Group, the Hotel shall provide one (1) complimentary room night at no charge to Group.

findings.finding_text: Commission is set at 9%, below CD's required 10% standard, and the contract does not address commission on cancellation damages collected by the Hotel, non-cancelable/non-transferable status, or commission surviving a change of brand/management at no less than 10%.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should pay ConferenceDirect 10% commission on all actualized room revenue, non-cancelable and non-transferable, surviving management/brand changes, and 10% of any cancellation damages collected.
findings.proposed_language: All rates confirmed in this Agreement are commissionable at ten percent (10%) to ConferenceDirect, LLC, regardless of rate paid and including all rooms outside the block. Commission is non-cancelable and non-transferable. Should Hotel change management company or brand affiliation, the new management will honor the existing 10% commission. Hotel will pay ConferenceDirect ten percent (10%) of any liquidated damages paid by Group within ten (10) days of receiving them.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel shall pay to Group a sales commission equal to nine percent (9%) of all room revenue actualized in connection with the Event

findings.finding_text: The finance charge on late undisputed balances is 1.3% per month, exceeding CD's cap of 1% per month or the legal maximum, whichever is less. The dispute window is only 12 days, shorter than CD's 30-day standard. The prepayment schedule for credit-denied Groups is a single 75% lump prepayment rather than CD's staged schedule (25%/25%/50%), and there is no provision for automatically extending credit if the Hotel never sends a credit application.
findings.cd_standard: Finance charges should be capped at 1% per month or the legal maximum, whichever is less; Group should have 30 days to dispute charges before finance charges accrue; if credit is denied, payment should follow a staged deposit schedule (25% at 14 business days after denial, 25% one month out, 50% three days before); and credit should be extended automatically if Hotel fails to send or follow up on a credit application.
findings.proposed_language: A finance charge not to exceed one percent (1.0%) per month, or the maximum allowed by law, whichever is less, will apply to unpaid, undisputed balances thirty (30) days after invoice. Group will have thirty (30) days from receipt of the final itemized invoice to dispute any charge before any finance charge accrues on the disputed amount. If credit is denied, Group will pay twenty-five percent (25%) of estimated charges within fourteen (14) business days of the denial, twenty-five percent (25%) one (1) month prior to the Event, and fifty percent (50%) three (3) days before the Event, rather than a single 75% prepayment. If Hotel fails to send Group a credit application or a written reminder to complete it, Hotel will extend credit to Group automatically.
findings.quoted_text: The Monarch shall assess a monthly finance charge of 1.3% on any portion of an undisputed invoice balance remaining unpaid thirty (30) days after the invoice due date.

findings.finding_text: The rate parity clause does not address the requirement that Group's rate be no higher than any other group's rate within 7 days either side of the event dates.
findings.cd_standard: The group's rate should also be no higher than any other group's rate within 7 days either side of the event.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel further agrees that Group's rate will be no higher than the group rate given to any other group over the period from seven (7) days before through seven (7) days after the room block dates.

findings.finding_text: The annual future-rate increase cap is 3%, exceeding CD's standard 2% cap, and final rates are confirmed 11 months prior rather than CD's 12-month standard.
findings.cd_standard: Room rate increases for future years should be capped at 2% per year, and final rates should be fixed in writing no later than 12 months before the event.
findings.proposed_language: The Hotel shall not increase the group room rates from year to year by more than two percent (2%) on an annual basis. The Group shall confirm all room rates as final twelve (12) months prior to the event dates.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel shall not increase the group room rates from year to year by more than three percent (3%) on an annual basis.

findings.finding_text: Although the Group may retain its own outside vendors, the clause imposes an outside vendor surcharge, contrary to CD's standard that vendor choice should carry no additional fee. (Note: the surcharge amount is listed as $0.00, which may effectively cure this — flagged for confirmation given the contradictory language imposing a surcharge obligation.)
findings.cd_standard: The group should be free to use the outside vendor of its choice at no additional fee or surcharge.
findings.proposed_language: Group reserves the right to utilize the supplier of its choice, at no additional service fee or surcharge, for services including but not limited to audio-visual, exhibit decorating, security, floral, transportation, and tours. Delete the outside vendor surcharge provision in its entirety.
findings.quoted_text: the Group shall remit to the Hotel an outside vendor surcharge in the amount of "$0.00". This surcharge shall be payable in full upon execution of this Agreement and represents the Hotel's sole additional compensation for the privilege of hosting outside vendors on the Hotel's premises during the Event.

findings.finding_text: The relocation clause does not provide the Hotel's commitment to contact Group in advance of a walk, to walk Group's attendees only after transient guests and other groups, or to honor a do-not-walk list of key attendees. It also lacks a per-room-night rebate to Group's master account for each relocated guest and provides no additional compensation threshold if the Hotel walks 10 or more guests or 10% or more of the peak-night block.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should contact the group in advance of any walk, walk attendees only after transient and other groups, honor a do-not-walk list, provide a per-room-night rebate to the group, and pay additional compensation for walking 10+ guests or 10%+ of peak-night block.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will contact Group in advance of any walk, will not walk members of Group before transient guests and other groups, and will review Group's attendee list with Group to identify those who cannot be walked. Hotel will credit Group's master account $[X] for each night a guest is relocated, regardless of that guest's rate. If Hotel walks ten (10) or more guests, or ten percent (10%) or more of the contracted peak-night block, Hotel will owe Group reasonable additional compensation.
findings.quoted_text: In the event that the Hotel is unable to honor all guaranteed reservations due to overbooking or operational circumstance, the Hotel shall relocate any affected guest to comparable or better accommodations

findings.finding_text: The threshold for a facility/service reduction triggering the Hotel's notice and alternative-offering obligation is 30% of stated capacity or scope, exceeding CD's 25% threshold.
findings.cd_standard: The threshold for triggering the hotel's obligation to offer alternatives or allow termination should be a reduction of more than 25% of published capacity or service ratio, not 30%.
findings.proposed_language: In the event that circumstances beyond the Hotel's reasonable control necessitate the temporary or permanent reduction, limitation, or discontinuation of any facility or service by more than twenty-five percent (25%) of its stated capacity or scope, the Hotel shall immediately notify Group in writing and propose alternative facilities or services.
findings.quoted_text: necessitate the temporary or permanent reduction, limitation, or discontinuation of any facility or service by more than thirty percent (30%) of its stated capacity or scope

findings.finding_text: The contract contains no clause naming specific function rooms with minimum square footage and ceiling height, no provision waiving room rental for meeting space in the program agenda, and no commitment to complimentary in-room AV basics (wired microphone, podium, power, lighting, HVAC).
findings.cd_standard: The contract should name each function room with minimum square footage/ceiling height, waive room rental for program-agenda meeting space, and provide complimentary basic AV/power/lighting/HVAC per room.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will hold the meeting and function space set out in Exhibit [X], with room rental charges waived, specifying each function space assignment, minimum square footage, and ceiling height requirement. No change will be made to function space assignments without written consent of both parties. Hotel will provide in each meeting room, at no charge, one wired microphone, a podium, power, proper lighting, and HVAC.

findings.finding_text: The contract does not specify minimum banquet staffing ratios for servers or bartenders at plated or buffet meals, nor address labor fees for small functions.
findings.cd_standard: The contract should guarantee minimum server-to-guest and bartender-to-guest ratios with no labor fee except for functions under 25 people.
findings.proposed_language: At all meal functions, Hotel will provide at least one server for every twenty-five (25) guests at a plated breakfast and every twenty (20) guests at a plated lunch or dinner, and one server for every forty (40) guests at a buffet breakfast and every thirty (30) guests at a buffet lunch or dinner, with no extra service charge for these ratios. Hotel will provide one bartender for every seventy-five (75) guests at hosted bars and one for every one hundred (100) guests at cash bars, with no bartender fees.

findings.finding_text: The contract contains no reference to honoring attached audio-visual or internet bandwidth quotes, no minimum bandwidth guarantee, and no discount commitment on additional AV/internet needs.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should honor attached AV and internet quotes, with a minimum bandwidth of 10 Mbps download/1 Mbps upload, and a discount on additional needs, with no tie to using the in-house AV provider for discounted internet.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will honor the pricing of the attached audio-visual quote and apply a discount of [X]% to any additional audio-visual needs, regardless of which provider is in place. Hotel will honor the attached internet bandwidth quote, providing a minimum of 10 Mbps download and 1 Mbps upload speed, with a discount of [X]% on additional needs. Use of Hotel's in-house audio-visual provider will not be a condition of any discounted or complimentary service, such as internet.

findings.finding_text: The clause states no deposit is charged and any damage funds held are applied only to documented damage (matching CD's standard on non-commingling), but there is no explicit 30-day refund window stated for any residual funds beyond 'within thirty (30) days of Group's departure should no damage occur' combined with damage documentation delivered within 30 days post-departure, creating a potential timing gap where refund could be delayed pending a 30-day damage documentation period plus a further dispute window.
findings.cd_standard: Any security or damage deposit should be refundable within a defined 30-day window absent documented, itemized damage.
findings.proposed_language: Any security deposit or funds held by Hotel for damage shall be refunded in full within thirty (30) days of Group's departure unless Hotel provides an itemized accounting of documented damage within that same period.
findings.quoted_text: Following such payment or within thirty (30) days of Group's departure should no damage occur, any remaining deposit shall be refunded to the billing contact on Group's master account.

findings.finding_text: The construction/renovation clause requires Group to exercise its termination right within only 10 business days of receiving notice of an interfering project, shorter than CD's standard 30-day window, and contains no provision for a new build or hotel reopening scenario (fully-operational date commitment, 5 business days' notice of change, damages if no suitable alternative venue found).
findings.cd_standard: Group should have 30 days to exercise its termination right after receiving notice of interfering construction, and for new builds/reopenings the hotel should commit to a fully-operational date with 5 business days' notice of change and damages coverage if no suitable alternative is found.
findings.proposed_language: If any renovation, construction, or capital project undertaken by the Hotel will materially interfere with Group's Event, Group may terminate this Agreement without liability, provided Group furnishes written notice within thirty (30) days of receiving notice of the interfering project.
findings.quoted_text: the Group may terminate this Agreement without penalty, liability, or further obligation, provided that the Group furnishes written notice of termination to the Hotel within ten (10) business days of receiving notice of the interfering project.

findings.finding_text: The Group's termination right upon change of brand/ownership/management is conditioned on Group demonstrating in good faith that the change materially affects the Hotel's performance or service standards, rather than being available at Group's discretion as CD's standard calls for. The notice deadline to the Hotel for disclosing the change (35 days after execution, or as promptly as practicable thereafter) is also looser than CD's 30-day-from-change standard, and Group's window to terminate is 25 days rather than 30.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should notify the group within 30 days of a change in ownership, management, or brand, and the group should be able to terminate without liability within 30 days of that notice, without needing to demonstrate materiality.
findings.proposed_language: Should Hotel undergo a material change in ownership, management company, or brand affiliation, or file for bankruptcy, or have foreclosure occur, Hotel will inform Group in writing within thirty (30) days of such change or filing. Group may, at its sole discretion, terminate this Agreement without liability within thirty (30) days of receiving that notice, without need to demonstrate material effect on Hotel's performance.
findings.quoted_text: provided that the Group demonstrating, in good faith, that the change materially affects the Hotel's ability to perform its obligations under this Agreement or materially alters the character or service standards of the property.

findings.finding_text: While the resale clause provides a mitigation duty and record access, cancellation damages are due within 30 days of receiving the cancellation notice rather than being deferred until 30 days after the meeting dates and contingent on the hotel showing evidence rooms went unsold, which reduces the practical benefit of the resale credit for damages assessed before the event even occurs.
findings.cd_standard: Cancellation damages should not fall due until 30 days after the meeting dates, and only once the hotel shows evidence of its mitigation effort and that rooms/space went unsold.
findings.proposed_language: Cancellation damages, if any, are due thirty (30) days after the Event's meeting dates, provided Hotel supplies reasonable evidence of its mitigation efforts and that the rooms and space held for Group went unsold.
findings.quoted_text: Hotel shall calculate the final damages due within thirty (30) days of receiving Group's cancellation notice and shall provide Group with a written accounting that itemizes the damages calculation, resale credits applied, and any remaining amount due.

analysis.document_notes: The contract is a complete, well-organized 29-section Group Sales Agreement with no illegible or missing pages. Several clauses (nondiscrimination, hotel_cancellation, review_audit_dates/reporting, assignment, reservation_procedures) largely track CD's standard language closely and no deviations were found for them. Signature blocks are unexecuted (dates/names blank). The outside vendor surcharge clause is internally contradictory (imposing a surcharge obligation but stating the amount as $0.00), which should be clarified/removed rather than left ambiguous. Exposure dollar amounts were largely left null because the contract does not provide enough concrete figures (e.g., final room block pickup, actual F&B spend) to calculate precise shortfalls; where the room rate ($419) and block size (210 rooms) were available, they were referenced qualitatively in proposed language but no confident dollar exposure was calculated without knowing actual pickup or F&B spend at time of review."

findings.finding_text: Attrition is measured night-by-night rather than cumulatively, the trigger threshold is 80% instead of 70%, damages are calculated at 80% of the full nightly room rate (not 70% lost-profit on the net group rate), nights hitting only 100% occupancy (not 95%+) get credit and only if Group's own rooms also fall below threshold, and Group is expressly denied any audit or dispute rights over the Hotel's attrition calculation, which is stated to be 'final and binding.' There is also no rebooking credit provision.
findings.cd_standard: Attrition liability should be calculated cumulatively across the entire block, triggered only below 70% pickup, at 70% lost profit on the single net group rate, with full credit for any night at 95%+ occupancy, audit rights for Group, and a rebooking credit if a CD client rebooks the hotel.
findings.proposed_language: Attrition liability, if any, will be calculated on a cumulative (not night-by-night) basis, with liability triggered only if Group's actual pickup falls below seventy percent (70%) of the total contracted room block. For each unsold room night below that threshold, Group will pay an amount equal to seventy percent (70%) (lost profit) of Group's single confirmed net group rate of $189.00 (plus tax, if required by applicable law). For any night the Hotel achieves 95% occupancy or higher, Group will receive full credit toward its block commitment for that night. At Group's request, Hotel will provide a copy of its city ledger or daily report showing the information needed to verify the calculation, and Group shall have the right to audit or dispute the Hotel's attrition determination. Should a ConferenceDirect client rebook the Hotel within [X] years, Hotel will credit up to 100% of the attrition damages paid toward the new booking.
findings.quoted_text: Attrition is measured on a night-by-night basis, and Group's block commitment is calculated as the total number of room nights reserved under the block minus attrition, if any.
findings.exposure_basis: 275 rooms x 80% rate ($189) x ~ up to full block shortfall exposure at 80% of rate rather than 70% lost profit, difference calculable only roughly; underlying figure: 275 rooms x $189 x 0.80 = $41,580 per night vs CD standard of 70% lost profit basis

findings.finding_text: Cancellation damages are based on gross room revenue rather than 70% lost-profit on the net group rate, the Hotel is not obligated to mitigate by reselling (and expressly retains all resale proceeds without credit), there is no rebooking credit, and Group is denied a liability-free cancellation window given the schedule starts at 20% even 365+ days out.
findings.cd_standard: Cancellation damages should be a sliding scale calculated against 70% lost room profit on the net group rate, with active mitigation duty and credited resale proceeds, plus a rebooking credit.
findings.proposed_language: In the event of cancellation, liquidated damages will be calculated as a percentage of room profit (defined as seventy percent (70%) of the confirmed single net group rate of $189.00) on the sliding scale set forth in Appendix A. Hotel will undertake all reasonable efforts to resell canceled rooms and will credit those revenues against the cancellation damages, not to exceed the full amount of such damages. Should a ConferenceDirect client rebook the Hotel within [X] years, Hotel will credit up to 100% of the cancellation damages paid toward the new booking's room revenue.
findings.quoted_text: Should Group cancel this Agreement in whole or in part at any time following the date of signature, Group shall be liable to the Hotel for liquidated damages calculated as a percentage of gross room revenue that would have been earned on the cancelled room nights.

findings.finding_text: The contract expressly relieves the Hotel of any duty to mitigate by reselling released rooms/function space, allows it to retain all resale proceeds without crediting Group, and bars Group from auditing or reviewing resale efforts or records.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should have an affirmative, documented duty to resell canceled rooms and credit proceeds against damages, with records available to Group to verify the effort.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will undertake all reasonable efforts to resell canceled rooms and function space, and will credit those revenues against any cancellation or attrition damages owed by Group. Hotel will document its mitigation efforts and make records available to Group upon request. Cancellation damages will be due only after Hotel supplies reasonable evidence of its mitigation effort and that the rooms held for Group went unsold.
findings.quoted_text: Upon release of rooms or function space by Group, the Hotel shall have no obligation to attempt to resell such released inventory, and Group waives any right to require the Hotel to undertake resale efforts or to mitigate damages through the placement of such space with alternative guests or groups.

findings.finding_text: The cutoff date is 45 days prior to arrival, beyond CD's 21-day standard, and after cutoff attendees are offered only rack rate with no group-rate continuation, no prepayment-hold option, and no consultation before releasing unassigned rooms.
findings.cd_standard: Cutoff should be no earlier than 21 days prior to arrival; after cutoff, attendees should continue to get the group rate as long as the hotel sells to the public or the room type remains available, and unassigned rooms should be handled via prepayment-hold, refund, or consultation before release.
findings.proposed_language: The cutoff date for the room block will be twenty-one (21) days prior to Group's arrival date. After the cutoff date, Group members may continue to reserve rooms at the group rate for as long as Hotel is selling rooms to the general public, regardless of room type. Hotel will consult with Group before releasing any unassigned rooms in the block for resale.
findings.quoted_text: All room reservations on behalf of Group must be requested and confirmed by the Hotel no later than forty-five (45) days prior to the Event check-in date of July 13, 2027.

findings.finding_text: Force majeure excuses performance only when it becomes 'physically impossible,' a much narrower bar than commercially impracticable/inadvisable/20% cancellation threshold, and it expressly excludes government-imposed travel restrictions and travel advisories of any kind. Deposits and prepayments are also expressly forfeited (retained in full by Hotel) rather than refunded, and there's no waiver of attrition/F&B/rental fees if Group holds a reduced event.
findings.cd_standard: Force majeure should allow cancellation where performance would be illegal, impossible, commercially impracticable, or inadvisable, or would cause 20%+ attendee cancellations, and should explicitly include government travel advisories/restrictions; deposits should be refunded promptly.
findings.proposed_language: Either party may cancel this Agreement without liability upon written notice to the other party should any cause beyond the control of Hotel or Group — including acts of God, war, terrorism, disease or epidemic, a CDC advisory, government travel advisory, government closures, or government/corporate/educational travel restrictions — make it, in that party's reasonable judgment, commercially impracticable, inadvisable, illegal, or impossible to perform, or cause 20% or more of Group's attendees to cancel or be reasonably anticipated to cancel. Hotel will refund all deposits and prepayments within five (5) business days of the notice of termination.
findings.quoted_text: Neither party shall be deemed in breach of this Agreement if performance becomes physically impossible due to an event beyond that party's reasonable control, including but not limited to acts of God, war, terrorism, civil unrest, labor strikes, or material failure of utilities or infrastructure. Notwithstanding the foregoing, neither government-imposed travel restrictions nor government travel advisories of any kind, whether mandatory or advisory in character, shall be deemed a force majeure event excusing or limiting the obligations of Group under this Agreement.

findings.finding_text: Any termination by Group for cause is expressly treated as a cancellation subject to the full liquidated-damages scale, contrary to CD's standard that termination for cause should carry no liability. There is also no separate list of qualifying causes (pandemic judgment, brand/ownership change, facility reduction, convention center unavailability, discriminatory legislation) giving Group a no-liability exit.
findings.cd_standard: Termination for cause should allow Group to walk away with no liability and a prompt refund, entirely separate from the cancellation damages scale, for causes including force majeure, pandemic judgment, labor dispute, ownership/brand change, renovation interference, facility reduction, convention center unavailability, and discriminatory legislation.
findings.proposed_language: Group may terminate this Agreement without liability, and Hotel will refund all deposits within five (5) days, upon: force majeure; Group's determination that an epidemic or pandemic affects its ability to hold the Event; a labor dispute involving Hotel's employees; a material change in Hotel's ownership, management, or brand; interfering renovation; a facility or service reduction not remedied within 30 days; unavailability of a relied-upon convention center or overflow hotel; or discriminatory state/local legislation. None of the foregoing will be treated as a cancellation under Article 8's liquidated damages scale.
findings.quoted_text: Any termination of this Agreement by the Group, irrespective of the cause or justification asserted by the Group, shall be treated as a cancellation by the Group under the cancellation damages scale set forth in Article 8, and the Group shall pay to the Hotel the cancellation damages calculated in accordance with that scale based on the date on which the termination notice is delivered.

findings.finding_text: The clause excludes bankruptcy, receivership, foreclosure, and assignment for benefit of creditors from triggering any notice or termination right, contrary to CD's standard that these events should trigger both notice and a termination right.
findings.cd_standard: If the hotel undergoes a change in ownership, management, brand, bankruptcy, or foreclosure, it should notify Group within 30 days and Group should be able to terminate without liability within 30 days of notice.
findings.proposed_language: Should Hotel undergo a material change in ownership, management company, or brand affiliation, or file for bankruptcy, or have foreclosure occur, Hotel will inform Group in writing within thirty (30) days of such change or filing. Group may terminate this Agreement without liability within thirty (30) days of receiving that notice, and Hotel will refund all deposits within five (5) days.
findings.quoted_text: Notwithstanding the foregoing, neither bankruptcy, receivership, foreclosure, assignment for benefit of creditors, nor any other proceedings or event arising from the financial distress or insolvency of Hotel or its parent, affiliate, or operating company shall trigger any notice obligation or afford Group any right of termination, cancellation, or offset, and Group's obligations hereunder shall remain in full force and effect regardless of any such development.

findings.finding_text: The Hotel is under no obligation to provide advance notice of CBA expiration or of an actual labor dispute, and Group is expressly denied any cancellation right or damages/credits arising from a labor dispute, strike, or lockout affecting the Hotel.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should provide a year's advance notice of CBA expirations and prompt notice of actual disputes; Group should be able to cancel without liability if a strike/lockout/expired contract arises within 90 days of the event.
findings.proposed_language: One year in advance, Hotel will provide Group in writing a list of all collective bargaining agreement expiration dates for the ensuing year, and will notify Group in writing within ten (10) working days after becoming aware of any labor dispute. If, within ninety (90) days prior to or during the Event, a strike, lockout, or expired labor contract occurs, Group may cancel this Agreement without liability, and any deposits will be promptly refunded.
findings.quoted_text: Hotel shall have no obligation to provide Group with advance notice, periodic reports, or any information concerning the expiration dates, renewal status, or negotiation schedule of any collective bargaining agreement, labor agreement, or labor arrangement applicable to Hotel's employees or operations, and Group hereby waives any right to receive such notice or information.

findings.finding_text: Group is required to use only Hotel's in-house or exclusively appointed vendors, with a $2,500 per-category surcharge for using an outside vendor, contrary to CD's standard of free vendor choice at no additional fee.
findings.cd_standard: Group should be free to use the outside vendor of its choice at no additional fee or surcharge.
findings.proposed_language: Group reserves the right to utilize the supplier of its choice, at no additional service fee or surcharge, for catering, audiovisual, floral, entertainment, and other services in connection with the Event. Hotel's in-house or preferred vendors are not mandatory for any service category.
findings.quoted_text: Group shall engage only the Hotel's in-house vendors or those exclusively appointed by the Hotel for catering, audiovisual equipment, floral arrangements, entertainment, and all other services provided in connection with the Event, except as expressly waived in writing by the Hotel's Director of Sales. Group's use of outside vendors not approved in advance by the Hotel shall be subject to a surcharge of $2,500.00 per outside vendor service or vendor category
findings.exposure_basis: $2,500 surcharge per outside vendor category if Group elects to use an outside vendor

findings.finding_text: Menu pricing is locked for 24 months rather than the 12-month maximum, and the shortfall on the F&B minimum is billed dollar-for-dollar (100%) rather than at 35% of the gap. There's also no provision counting affiliate/exhibitor F&B revenue toward the minimum.
findings.cd_standard: F&B minimums should lock pricing no earlier than 12 months out, and any shortfall should be billed at 35% of the gap, with affiliate/exhibitor revenue counting toward the minimum.
findings.proposed_language: Menu prices for the Event's food and beverage functions will be confirmed not earlier than twelve (12) months prior to the Event. If actual food and beverage revenue is less than the guaranteed minimum, Group will pay Hotel thirty-five percent (35%) of the difference between actual revenue and the minimum, not the full shortfall. Food and beverage revenue from all affiliate organizations and exhibitors meeting in conjunction with Group's Event will count toward the minimum.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel shall provide to the Group a menu and pricing proposal that shall remain binding as to pricing for a period of twenty-four (24) months from the date of this Agreement

findings.finding_text: Gratuity and service charge are conflated as interchangeable and undefined terms, with the Hotel retaining sole discretion to keep the entire 24% as its own revenue rather than distributing gratuity to staff, contrary to CD's standard requiring clear, separate definition and full distribution of gratuity to staff.
findings.cd_standard: Gratuity and service charge should be clearly and separately defined and confirmed in the contract, with gratuity fully distributed to staff and any separate service charge disclosed as hotel revenue.
findings.proposed_language: [X]% of the food and beverage total, plus applicable tax, will be added to Group's account as a gratuity and will be fully distributed to the servers, bussers, and bartenders assigned to the Event. A separate service charge of [X]%, plus applicable tax, is distinct from gratuity, is not distributed as a tip, and is retained by Hotel to cover discretionary costs of the Event. Both percentages are confirmed in this Agreement.
findings.quoted_text: The terms 'gratuity' and 'service charge' are used interchangeably throughout this Agreement and do not constitute separately defined charges.

findings.finding_text: The Hotel may assess additional fees at any time in its sole discretion post-signature, and Group remains liable even for fees never disclosed prior to execution — the opposite of CD's standard. A $35/night non-negotiable resort fee is also imposed with no waiver option.
findings.cd_standard: All charges must be disclosed in writing before signature; any undisclosed charge should be waived, and later add-ons need Group's written approval; resort fees should be waived for attendees while services are still honored.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will disclose in writing, prior to execution of this Agreement, all charges associated with the Event, including resort fees, surcharges, technology fees, and administrative costs. Any charge not disclosed to Group in writing prior to signature is waived. Should Group require additional services after signature, Hotel must obtain Group's written approval before providing the service and before posting the charge. Hotel will waive the $35.00 per-night resort fee for all attendees while continuing to honor the resort fee services.
findings.quoted_text: Notwithstanding any other provision, Group remains liable for all charges assessed by Hotel, whether or not such charges were disclosed in writing prior to execution of this Agreement. Hotel's failure to disclose any fee or surcharge before signature shall not relieve Group of its obligation to pay such charge upon invoice.

findings.finding_text: The complimentary room ratio is 1:80 (versus CD's 1:40), is stated as a mere non-binding guideline subject to Hotel's sole discretion, is entirely forfeited (not prorated) for any pickup shortfall, and there is no provision crediting no-show/cancellation fees or miscoded rooms toward pickup, nor complimentary in-room internet.
findings.cd_standard: Complimentary rooms should be earned on a clear, cumulative 1:40 formula tied to actual pickup, not forfeited due to attrition, with no-shows/cancellation fees and miscoded rooms counting toward pickup, and complimentary in-room internet regardless of loyalty status.
findings.proposed_language: Group will receive one (1) complimentary room for every forty (40) occupied, revenue-producing room nights actualized, calculated cumulatively across the entire room block, regardless of whether the contracted block was otherwise met. Each no-show fee and cancellation fee charged will be credited as one (1) room night toward Group's pickup. Hotel will provide complimentary internet in attendees' guest rooms regardless of loyalty program participation.
findings.quoted_text: Hotel shall consider providing complimentary guestroom accommodations to Group at a ratio of one (1) complimentary room for every eighty (80) occupied rooms successfully billed during the Event, provided Group achieves full pickup of its contracted room block. The complimentary room ratio stated herein is a guideline only and does not constitute a commitment or guarantee of any specific number of complimentary rooms.

findings.finding_text: The Hotel reserves an unrestricted right to sell rooms below Group's rate with no retroactive adjustment for existing reservations, and any adjusted rate offered is expressly non-commissionable and excluded from pickup/rebate calculations, contrary to CD's standard.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should guarantee it won't undercut the group's rate, or if it does, adjust the rate retroactively (or count all attendee bookings in the block regardless of rate) while preserving commission and pickup credit.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel guarantees it will not sell guestrooms at a rate lower than Group's contracted rate during the Event dates, except qualified rates (government, airline, contracted corporate). If Hotel offers a lower rate, Hotel will adjust the rate for all prior reservations in Group's block to match. Commission will be paid on the contracted rate regardless of adjustment, and such rooms remain creditable toward Group's pickup and complimentary-room calculations.
findings.quoted_text: Any adjusted rate made available to Group following identification of a lower public rate shall be treated as a non-commissionable rate and shall not be credited toward Group's room block pickup, occupancy targets, or performance metrics for purposes of calculating complimentary rooms, rebates, or other volume-based benefits under this Agreement.

findings.finding_text: Group is given no dispute window before finance charges apply, and the finance charge (1.5% monthly, compounded) exceeds CD's 1%-per-month cap; payment is due in only 15 days rather than upon receipt with a real dispute window.
findings.cd_standard: Master account should be payable upon receipt of invoice with a real dispute window before finance charges apply, and any finance charge should be capped at 1% per month or the legal max, whichever is less.
findings.proposed_language: The master account is payable upon receipt of invoice. Group will have thirty (30) days from receipt of the final itemized invoice to review and dispute any charge in good faith before any finance charge accrues. If payment of undisputed charges is not received within thirty (30) days of the final invoice, a finance charge not to exceed one percent (1.0%) per month, or the maximum allowed by law, whichever is less, will apply to the unpaid, undisputed balance.
findings.quoted_text: All invoiced amounts shall be due and payable in full when due, with no period in which Group may dispute a charge. Invoices shall be submitted by Hotel to Group's designated billing contact within thirty (30) days following the Event, and payment shall be due within fifteen (15) days of invoice date. Hotel shall have the right to charge a monthly finance charge of 1.5% on the outstanding balance, compounded monthly, until such amount is paid in full.

findings.finding_text: The $25,000 security deposit is expressly commingled and applied against attrition charges, F&B shortfalls, and cancellation fees (not just documented property damage), refund window is 90 days rather than 30, and no interest or itemized-damage requirement is specified beyond Hotel's own discretion.
findings.cd_standard: Security deposits should be reasonable, refunded within 30 days absent documented itemized damage, and not commingled with or offset against attrition or F&B minimum shortfalls.
findings.proposed_language: The security deposit will be refunded in full within thirty (30) days of the Event's conclusion unless Hotel provides an itemized accounting of specific, documented damage caused by Group or its attendees beyond normal wear and tear. The deposit may not be applied toward attrition, cancellation, or F&B minimum shortfalls.
findings.quoted_text: Hotel shall apply the deposit, in its sole discretion, against attrition charges, food and beverage shortfalls, damage to Hotel property, unpaid room charges, cancellation fees, or any other amounts owed by Group to Hotel under this Agreement or otherwise.
findings.exposure_basis: Full security deposit amount stated in Section 15

findings.finding_text: Walked guests must arrange and pay for their own alternative lodging and transportation, receive no upgrade or welcome amenity on return, and the relocated night is expressly excluded from Group's pickup and commission calculation — the opposite of CD's standard across every element.
findings.cd_standard: Walked guests should get comparable-or-better accommodations and round-trip transportation at Hotel's expense, plus an upgrade and welcome amenity on return; the relocated night should count toward pickup and commission with no attrition liability, and extra compensation if 10+ guests or 10%+ of peak night are walked.
findings.proposed_language: For each displaced guest, Hotel will, at its own expense: (a) provide accommodations at a comparable or better hotel; (b) provide complimentary round-trip transportation between the Hotel and alternate hotel; (c) forward messages, mail, and packages; and (d) provide an upgrade and welcome amenity upon return. Each displaced room will be credited toward Group's pickup and commission base, and Group will not be liable for attrition damages for any night a guest is walked. If Hotel walks ten (10) or more guests or ten percent (10%) or more of the contracted peak-night block, Hotel will owe Group reasonable additional compensation.
findings.quoted_text: The affected guest shall bear full responsibility for all transportation costs to and from any alternative hotel arranged pursuant to a walk relocation. Hotel shall not provide, arrange, or reimburse transportation between the Hotel and any substitute facility, and guests shall make their own arrangements for such travel at their sole cost and expense.

findings.finding_text: The Hotel disclaims any representation about renovation, may commence work at any time including during the Event with no advance notice, and Group waives any right to terminate, claim damages, or seek any remedy for disruption — contrary to CD's standard of no-interference representations, 30 days' notice, and a termination right if the work will interfere.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should represent no current renovation plans affecting group space, commit to 30 days' notice of confirmed work with mitigation plan, and let Group terminate without liability if it determines the work will interfere.
findings.proposed_language: As of this Agreement's date, Hotel has no plans for renovation affecting facilities Group will use, other than ordinary maintenance. If Hotel later confirms such plans, it will notify Group in writing within thirty (30) days, describing scope, schedule, anticipated impact, and mitigation plan. If Group determines the work will interfere with its meeting, Group may terminate this Agreement without liability upon written notice within thirty (30) days of receiving Hotel's plans.
findings.quoted_text: Hotel shall have the right to commence renovation work at the Hotel at any time, including during the Event, without providing Group advance notice of any kind, and Group shall have no right to object to or restrict such work based on timing, noise, dust, disruption, or any other impact on Group's event or its attendees.
