findings.finding_text: Indemnification runs one way only — Group indemnifies Hotel, including for Hotel's own ordinary and gross negligence, with the Hotel bearing no reciprocal indemnity obligation to Group at all — directly contrary to CD's mutual, negligence-limited standard.
findings.cd_standard: Indemnification should be mutual and limited to each party's own negligence or willful misconduct; the group should never indemnify the hotel for the hotel's own negligence.
findings.proposed_language: To the extent permitted by law, each party will indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the other party against claims arising out of the negligence or willful misconduct of the indemnifying party, its employees, agents, or contractors. Neither party indemnifies the other for that other party's own negligence. This provision survives termination of this Agreement.
findings.quoted_text: Group's indemnity obligations extend to and include claims arising from the Hotel's own negligence, ordinary or gross, provided that Group shall not be obligated to indemnify the Hotel for claims arising solely from the Hotel's gross negligence or willful misconduct.

findings.finding_text: Auxiliary aid costs are described as 'shared' with Group bearing incremental/specialized costs and Hotel only baseline costs, rather than the clean division where Group funds aids in its function space and Hotel funds aids in guest rooms/common areas as CD's standard requires; there's also no mutual ADA indemnification.
findings.cd_standard: Each party should indemnify only for its own ADA obligations, with Group funding auxiliary aids in function space it holds and Hotel funding aids in guest rooms and common areas.
findings.proposed_language: Group is responsible for obtaining and funding any auxiliary aids needed in the function space held for its use; Hotel is responsible for obtaining and funding any auxiliary aids required by law in guest rooms, public space, and common areas. Hotel and Group will each indemnify the other from liability arising from that party's own obligations under the ADA.
findings.quoted_text: the costs of such auxiliary aids shall be shared between Group and the Hotel. The Hotel shall provide baseline auxiliary aids that are considered standard for its operations, while Group shall bear responsibility for the incremental cost of specialized or unusual accommodations tailored specifically to the Event

findings.finding_text: Governing law and venue are set to the Hotel's location (Indiana/Marion County) rather than Group's location, the Hotel — but not Group — is entitled to recover punitive/exemplary/consequential damages, and the prevailing party (effectively favoring Hotel given asymmetric drafting) recovers attorney's fees rather than each side bearing its own.
findings.cd_standard: Governing law and venue should be the state/city where Group is located, with no punitive damages and each party bearing its own attorney's fees.
findings.proposed_language: This Agreement will be construed in accordance with the laws of the state in which Group is located. Any unresolved dispute will be settled by a court of law in the city in which Group is located. Any award will be limited to actual damages; punitive damages will not be awarded to either party. Each party will be responsible for its own attorney's fees and expenses.
findings.quoted_text: The Group consents to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in Marion County, Indiana, and waives any objection to venue or claim of inconvenient forum in any action or proceeding arising from or relating to this Agreement or the Event.

findings.finding_text: The Hotel expressly reserves the right to use Attendee Information for its own marketing purposes and to share it with affiliates/marketing partners without Group's consent, contrary to CD's standard limiting use to reservation fulfillment.
findings.cd_standard: Attendee data should be used solely to fulfill reservations, not for the hotel's own marketing or shared with third parties without Group's consent.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will use rooming list and Attendee Information solely for the purpose of fulfilling reservations and performing this Agreement. Hotel will not use such data for its own marketing purposes, nor disclose it to any third party, without Group's prior written consent.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel may use Attendee Information for its own marketing purposes, including but not limited to direct mail, email, and telephonic solicitation of the attendees who registered for the Event.

findings.finding_text: Group is expressly denied any right to audit or independently verify room block/pickup records or to engage a third-party auditor, and pickup reports are furnished only at Hotel's discretion rather than on a defined weekly/final schedule; there is also no requirement to credit miscoded or brand-rate rooms toward pickup.
findings.cd_standard: Group should have a no-cost room-block audit right comparing the hotel's guest list against Group's registration list, weekly pickup reports, and credit for miscoded rooms toward pickup.
findings.proposed_language: At Group's request and at no cost, Hotel will compare its in-house guest list against Group's registration list, either jointly with a Group representative or by permitting a ConferenceDirect or Group representative to do so independently. Hotel will provide Group a weekly guestroom pickup report and a final pickup report with supporting documentation within ten (10) days of departure. Any guest room occupied by an individual on Group's registration list but not coded to Group will be credited to Group's pickup regardless of rate paid.
findings.quoted_text: Group shall have no right to audit, inspect, or independently verify the room block records maintained by the Hotel, nor shall Group have any right to engage a third-party auditor or representative to examine the Hotel's reservation systems, registration records, or billing documentation.

findings.finding_text: Assignment to a successor management company or affiliated entity is barred without Hotel's sole and unreviewable discretion to withhold consent, contrary to CD's standard permitting assignment to a successor/affiliate without unreasonably withheld consent.
findings.cd_standard: Group should be able to assign the contract to a successor management company or affiliated entity without the hotel's consent being unreasonably withheld.
findings.proposed_language: Group may assign this Agreement to a successor association management company or affiliated entity without Hotel's consent, provided the assignee assumes all obligations under this Agreement and the event dates, room block, and program remain substantially unchanged. Any other assignment requires Hotel's consent, not to be unreasonably withheld.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel's consent to any proposed assignment or transfer shall be entirely within the Hotel's sole and absolute discretion, and the Hotel may withhold consent to an assignment for any reason whatsoever or for no reason stated.

findings.finding_text: The Agreement contains no provision addressing the Hotel's liability if it cancels the Agreement without a contractual right to do so — an omission that leaves Group with no assurance of recovering direct, indirect, and consequential damages if the Hotel walks away from the deal.
findings.cd_standard: If the hotel cancels without a right to do so under the contract, it should owe the group all direct, indirect, and consequential damages, not just a refund of deposits.
findings.proposed_language: In the event Hotel cancels this Agreement other than as permitted under this Agreement, Hotel will pay Group for all direct, indirect, and consequential damages, expenses, attorney's fees, and costs incurred by Group on account of such cancellation, including but not limited to staff time and travel expenses to secure an alternate location, incremental room rate and airfare differentials, function space rental, and communication and printing costs.

findings.finding_text: No provision addresses a future-rate cap or a decline-tracking discount, though not squarely applicable since this Agreement locks in a single confirmed group rate rather than deferred pricing; nonetheless, CD's standard calling for this protection where rates are not yet confirmed is absent given the 24-month binding menu/F&B pricing period referenced elsewhere suggests longer lead times are contemplated.
findings.cd_standard: Where room rates for a future year are not yet confirmed, the contract should cap any increase at 2% per year and lower the rate if market/published rates decline, fixed no later than 12 months before the event.
findings.proposed_language: Definite room rates are confirmed in writing in this Agreement. To the extent any rate component remains subject to future confirmation, Hotel guarantees a maximum yearly increase of two percent (2%) over rates quoted, and will discount the group rate if the market average rate for comparable hotels declines before arrival.

findings.finding_text: The Agreement contains no guarantee of minimum staffing ratios (servers, bartenders) at food and beverage functions, and no cap limiting labor fees to only small functions under 25 people.
findings.cd_standard: The contract should guarantee minimum server and bartender staffing ratios at F&B functions with no labor fee for meeting those ratios, and a labor fee only for functions under 25 people.
findings.proposed_language: At all meal functions, Hotel will provide at least one server for every twenty-five (25) guests at a plated breakfast and every twenty (20) guests at a plated lunch or dinner, and one server for every forty (40) guests at a buffet breakfast and every thirty (30) guests at a buffet lunch or dinner, with no extra service or labor charge for these ratios. Hotel will provide no fewer than one (1) bartender for every seventy-five (75) guests at hosted bars and one (1) bartender for every one hundred (100) guests at cash bars, with no bartender or service fees. There will be no special labor or service fees for any Group food or beverage function, except functions of fewer than twenty-five (25) people.

findings.finding_text: The Agreement contains no provision honoring an attached AV or internet bandwidth quote, no minimum bandwidth guarantee, and no discount commitment for later additions, nor a bar on tying discounted internet to use of the in-house AV vendor.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should honor AV and internet bandwidth quotes attached at contracting, guarantee at least 10 Mbps download/1 Mbps upload, discount later additions, and not condition discounted services on using the in-house AV provider.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will honor the pricing of the attached audio-visual quote and will apply a discount of [X]% to any additional audio-visual needs regardless of provider. Hotel will provide a minimum of 10 Mbps download and 1 Mbps upload internet bandwidth, with a discount of [X]% on additional needs. Use of Hotel's in-house audio-visual provider will not be a condition of any discounted or complimentary service, such as internet.

findings.finding_text: The Agreement contains no provisions on reservation confirmations, name changes at group rate, individual cancellation deadlines/fees, no-show reinstatement, or crediting individual cancellation money against Group's attrition liability.
findings.cd_standard: Reservation handling should favor attendees with prompt confirmations, name changes at group rate, a 6pm-day-of-arrival cancellation window, no-show reinstatement, and crediting of individual cancellation money against Group's attrition.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will send each registered guest confirmation of their reservation at no charge within four (4) days of receiving the information. Name changes may be made at the group rate up to the arrival date. No cancellation fee will be assessed for any room cancelled before 6:00 p.m. on the day of arrival. Hotel will reinstate no-shows for the following night at the same rate unless Group directs otherwise. Any individual cancellation money Hotel receives will be credited toward any attrition damages owed by Group.

findings.finding_text: The Agreement contains no provision addressing what happens if the Hotel closes or materially reduces restaurants, spa, fitness, or other facilities/services, leaving Group without recourse if such reductions occur before or during the Event.
findings.cd_standard: If the hotel closes or materially limits facilities or reduces staffing ratios by more than 25%, it should first offer equal alternatives, and Group should be able to cancel without liability if no resolution is reached within 30 days.
findings.proposed_language: If Hotel closes or limits the hours or capacity of any restaurant, health club, spa, fitness facility, contracted meeting space, or other venue by more than twenty-five percent (25%), or materially reduces service staffing ratios, Hotel will first offer equal alternative facilities or services at its own expense. If no mutually agreeable alternative is reached within thirty (30) days, Group may cancel this Agreement without liability.

findings.finding_text: The Agreement contains no named function room assignments, minimum square footage, ceiling height requirements, or commitment that meeting space in the program agenda is complimentary with no room rental, nor any commitment to complimentary in-room AV basics like microphone, podium, power, lighting, and HVAC.
findings.cd_standard: The contract should name each function room with square footage and ceiling height, commit that changes require both parties' written consent, waive room rental for program-agenda space, and provide basic AV/power/lighting/HVAC at no charge.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will hold the meeting and function space set out in an attached room specification, with room rental charges waived for space in Group's program agenda, and will specify each function space assignment, minimum square footage, and ceiling height requirement. No change will be made to function space assignments without written consent of both parties. Hotel will provide in each meeting room, at no charge, one wired microphone, a podium, power, proper lighting, and HVAC.

findings.finding_text: The Agreement contains no nondiscrimination commitment protecting attendees, and no termination right if state or local legislation permits discrimination against attendees.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should commit that it and its staff will not discriminate against attendees on protected grounds, and Group should be able to terminate without liability if state/local legislation permits such discrimination.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel agrees that Hotel and its employees and agents will not discriminate against any of Group's attendees on the basis of sex, gender identity or expression, age, race, color, religion, national or ethnic origin, disability, sexual orientation, genetic information, or parental, marital, military, or veteran status. Should the state of Indiana or the city of Indianapolis adopt legislation that affirmatively allows such discrimination, Group may terminate this Agreement without liability.

findings.finding_text: The named-storm cancellation window is extremely narrow: the warning must still be in effect within 24 hours of arrival and Group must give notice no later than 24 hours before arrival, whereas CD's standard uses a 72-hour forecast/notice window, giving Group far less time to act and less protection against an approaching storm.
findings.cd_standard: A named-storm clause should allow cancellation without liability when a storm is forecast to affect the hotel's location within 72 hours of any event date, regardless of whether the storm ultimately causes damage.
findings.proposed_language: In the event a named storm (hurricane, tropical storm, or severe winter storm) is forecast to affect the Hotel's location within 72 hours of any event date, either party may cancel the affected portion of the event without liability upon written or verbal (followed by written) notice, regardless of whether the storm ultimately causes physical damage to the Hotel.
findings.quoted_text: If the National Weather Service issues a named storm warning for the geographic area in which the Hotel is located at any time during the period commencing twenty-four (24) hours before the start of the Event and continuing through the final day of the Event, and if such warning remains in effect as of twenty-four (24) hours prior to the scheduled arrival date of Group

findings.finding_text: The Agreement contains no commission provision to ConferenceDirect at all — no rate, payment timing, or protection for commission on actualized room revenue, walked rooms, or cancellation damages.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should pay ConferenceDirect 10% commission on all actualized room revenue within 30 days of departure, including walked rooms and miscoded rooms, plus 10% of any cancellation damages collected.
findings.proposed_language: All rates confirmed in this Agreement are commissionable at ten percent (10%) to ConferenceDirect, LLC. Hotel will pay commission on all actualized room revenue, regardless of rate paid, within thirty (30) days of Group's departure, whether or not the master account has been paid in full. Hotel will pay ConferenceDirect ten percent (10%) of any liquidated damages paid by Group within ten (10) days of receiving them.

analysis.document_notes: The Agreement is heavily one-sided in favor of the Hotel across nearly every clause reviewed, with repeated language expressly denying Group audit rights, dispute rights, and mitigation protections that CD's standard positions treat as baseline. Several clauses reference exhibits/appendices (Appendix A cancellation schedule, Exhibit B F&B projection, a room block addendum) that were not provided in the text supplied for review and could not be independently verified. Numbering is inconsistent (Article 7 is referenced within Section 9's F&B clause but the actual gratuity/service charge article is Section 10; Section 8 termination-for-cause references "Article 8" for cancellation damages, which is actually Section 4) — these internal cross-reference errors should be flagged to the property for correction regardless of substantive findings.

findings.finding_text: The F&B shortfall is calculated as 35% of Group's total room revenue for the Event period, rather than 35% of the shortfall between actual F&B revenue and the F&B minimum. This ties the penalty to room revenue instead of the F&B gap itself, and there's no mention of affiliate/exhibitor F&B revenue counting toward the minimum.
findings.cd_standard: Any shortfall should be billed at 35% of the gap between actual F&B revenue and the minimum, not tied to room revenue, and affiliate/exhibitor F&B revenue should count toward the minimum.
findings.proposed_language: If actual food and beverage revenue is less than the minimum, Group will pay Hotel thirty-five percent (35%) of the difference between actual food and beverage revenue and the minimum commitment, not a percentage of room revenue. Food and beverage revenue from all affiliate organizations and exhibitors meeting in conjunction with Group's event will count toward the minimum.
findings.quoted_text: The shortfall shall be calculated as thirty-five percent (35%) of the Group's total room revenue for the Event period.

findings.finding_text: The contract mandates use of Hotel's in-house or exclusively-appointed vendors for AV, telecom, floral, décor, and entertainment, and imposes a $3,200 per-vendor surcharge if Group wants to use an outside vendor.
findings.cd_standard: Group should be free to use the outside vendor of its choice for these service categories at no additional fee or surcharge.
findings.proposed_language: Group reserves the right to utilize the supplier of its choice, at no additional service fee or surcharge, for services or rentals including but not limited to audio-visual, telecommunications, floral, décor, and entertainment. Hotel's in-house or exclusively-appointed vendors are not mandatory for any service category, and no surcharge will apply to Group's use of an outside vendor.
findings.quoted_text: Group shall engage the Hotel's in-house vendors or vendors with whom the Hotel maintains exclusive appointments for all ancillary services required in connection with the Event, including but not limited to audiovisual services, telecommunications, floral arrangements, décor, and entertainment. Any request by Group to retain an outside vendor not approved by the Hotel in writing shall be subject to a surcharge of $3,200.00 per outside vendor, which surcharge shall be payable by Group to the Hotel within ten (10) days of invoice.

findings.finding_text: The audit right conditions the cost of the audit on the outcome (Group pays if Hotel's records are accurate, Hotel pays only if material discrepancies found), which discourages Group from exercising the audit right at all, and is not present in CD's standard which calls for a no-cost or unconditional audit mechanism. There is no dollar-for-dollar credit between excess F&B revenue and room attrition damages, and no rebate-back provision if a CD client rebooks the Hotel.
findings.cd_standard: Group should have audit rights without penalty, excess F&B revenue above the minimum should be credited dollar for dollar against room attrition damages and vice versa, and damages paid should be credited back if a ConferenceDirect client later rebooks the hotel.
findings.proposed_language: At Group's request, Hotel will provide, at no cost to Group, its city ledger or daily occupancy report needed to verify the attrition calculation, regardless of the outcome of any such review. Any excess food and beverage revenue above Group's F&B minimum will be credited dollar-for-dollar against room attrition damages, and vice versa. Should a ConferenceDirect client rebook the Hotel for another meeting within two (2) years, Hotel will credit up to 100% of the attrition damages paid toward the new booking's room revenue, not to exceed the damages paid; if the rebooking group is not the group that paid, the credit will be refunded directly to the group that paid.
findings.quoted_text: Any audit shall be conducted at Group's expense if the Hotel's records are found to be accurate, and at the Hotel's expense if material discrepancies are discovered.

findings.finding_text: The force majeure clause does not explicitly extend to Group's right to cancel where 20% or more of attendees cancel or are reasonably anticipated to cancel, and does not address the scenario where Group instead holds a smaller meeting (waiver of attrition/F&B/rental fees and offering the lowest rate). It also caps damages recovery to a refund of deposits with no explicit statement that Group's invocation right is not limited by the party's awareness of the condition at signing.
findings.cd_standard: Force majeure should explicitly include a 20%-attendee-cancellation trigger, preserve the right regardless of knowledge at signing, and if Group holds a smaller meeting instead, the hotel should waive attrition, F&B, and rental fees and offer the lowest rate it offers anyone.
findings.proposed_language: Either party may cancel this Agreement without liability upon written notice to the other party should any qualifying cause make it commercially impracticable, inadvisable (including for health or safety reasons), illegal, or impossible to perform, or cause twenty percent (20%) or more of Group's attendees to cancel, or cause Group to reasonably anticipate that twenty percent (20%) or more of its attendees will cancel. Group's right to invoke this clause is not limited by either party's awareness of the condition when this Agreement was signed. If Group elects to hold the Event despite such circumstances at a reduced size, Hotel will waive any fees related to the reduced-size Event, including room and food and beverage attrition and function space rental, and will offer Group's attendees any lower room rate offered to other guests over the contracted dates.
findings.quoted_text: Force majeure events shall also include conditions that render it unsafe or imprudent for meeting attendees to travel to or gather at the Hotel, whether due to health risks, infrastructure damage, or other circumstances beyond the parties' reasonable control.

findings.finding_text: There is no provision counting miscoded rooms or no-show/cancellation fee room nights toward the complimentary room pickup calculation, and no mention of complimentary in-room internet regardless of loyalty status.
findings.cd_standard: Every occupied room should count toward pickup, including miscoded rooms and one room night for each no-show or cancellation fee charged, and attendees should get complimentary in-room internet regardless of loyalty-program status.
findings.proposed_language: All occupied rooms will be counted toward Group's pickup for purposes of the complimentary room calculation, including rooms credited to Group through a room block audit. Each no-show fee and each cancellation fee charged will be credited as one (1) room night toward Group's pickup and used in calculating complimentary rooms. Hotel will provide complimentary internet in attendees' guest rooms, regardless of brand loyalty program participation.
findings.quoted_text: Group shall receive complimentary rooms based on a ratio of one (1) complimentary room for every forty (40) paid rooms occupied during the event dates of April 26-29, 2027.

findings.finding_text: There is no 24-month and 12-month written room block review with the ability for Group to adjust the block up or down by a set percentage at the group rate, and the weekly pickup report begins only 8 weeks (56 days) prior to the event rather than a defined earlier window; miscoded rooms at brand-associate or business rates are not addressed for pickup crediting.
findings.cd_standard: The room block should be reviewed in writing at approximately 24 and 12 months out with Group able to adjust the block by a set percentage at the group rate, and any miscoded room, including at brand-associate or business rates, should be credited to Group's pickup regardless of rate paid.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel and Group will review the room block in writing approximately twenty-four (24) months prior to arrival and again approximately twelve (12) months prior. At Group's sole discretion, Group may increase or decrease the room block by up to [X]% at each review at the group rate. Any guest room occupied by an individual on Group's registration list but not coded to Group within Hotel's system — including rooms booked at qualified brand-associate or business rates or through Internet distribution channels — will be credited to Group's pickup regardless of the rate paid or reservation method.

findings.finding_text: Insurance is imposed solely on Group ($1,000,000 general liability naming Hotel as additional insured), with no reciprocal obligation for Hotel to carry insurance protecting its own activities.
findings.cd_standard: Insurance should be a mutual obligation, with each party carrying adequate insurance to protect its own activities, rather than a requirement imposed on the group alone.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel and Group will each carry adequate insurance to protect its own activities against claims arising out of the Event. Group shall maintain general liability insurance with minimum limits of $1,000,000.00 per occurrence, with the Hotel named as additional insured, and shall provide certificates of insurance to the Hotel at least thirty (30) days prior to the Event.
findings.quoted_text: Group shall maintain general liability insurance with minimum limits of $1,000,000.00 per occurrence, with the Hotel named as additional insured, and shall provide certificates of insurance to the Hotel at least thirty (30) days prior to the Event.

findings.finding_text: Termination for cause is defined only generically ('for cause') without enumerating the specific grounds CD's standard calls for (epidemic/pandemic judgment by Group, labor dispute, brand/ownership change, renovation interference, facility/service reduction, convention center unavailability, discriminatory legislation).
findings.cd_standard: Termination for cause should enumerate specific qualifying causes including force majeure, Group's own judgment on epidemic/pandemic, labor disputes, ownership/brand change, renovation interference, facility/service reductions, convention center/overflow hotel unavailability, and discriminatory legislation, all without triggering cancellation damages.
findings.proposed_language: Group may terminate this Agreement without liability, and Hotel will refund all deposits and prepayments within five (5) days, upon any of the following: (a) force majeure as defined in this Agreement; (b) Group's determination that an infectious disease outbreak, epidemic, or pandemic is affecting Group's ability to hold the Event as intended; (c) a labor dispute involving Hotel's employees arising within ninety (90) days of or during the Event; (d) a material change in Hotel's ownership, management company, or brand affiliation, or Hotel's bankruptcy or foreclosure; (e) renovation or remodeling that Group determines will interfere with its meeting; (f) a reduction in Hotel's facilities or services for which no mutually agreeable alternative is reached within thirty (30) days; (g) the convention center or overflow hotels on which the Event depends not being open, available, and fully operational over the Event dates; or (h) the adoption of state or local legislation that permits discrimination against attendees. None of the foregoing triggers the liquidated-damages calculation in the cancellation clause.

findings.finding_text: Gratuity and service charge are conflated as a single, undefined 25% charge, with the Hotel retaining sole discretion over allocation and no obligation to distribute any portion to staff — the contract expressly states the Hotel is not required to distribute the charge as gratuity, and does not disclose the split between staff compensation and Hotel revenue.
findings.cd_standard: Gratuity and service charge should be clearly and separately defined, with both percentages confirmed in the contract: gratuity should be fully distributed to staff, while a separate service charge should be disclosed as Hotel revenue rather than left ambiguous or presented as a tip.
findings.proposed_language: A gratuity of [X]% of the food and beverage total, plus applicable tax, will be added to Group's account and fully distributed to the servers, and where applicable, bussers and bartenders assigned to the Event. A separate service charge of [X]%, plus applicable tax, is distinct from gratuity, is not distributed as a tip, and is retained by Hotel to cover the discretionary costs of the Event. Both percentages, totaling twenty-five percent (25%), are confirmed and itemized separately in this Agreement.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel retains sole discretion to determine the allocation and distribution of any gratuity collected on behalf of Group, and the Hotel may retain such gratuity as Hotel revenue without obligation to distribute it to service staff.

findings.finding_text: The finance charge on late undisputed balances is set at 2% per month compounded monthly, exceeding CD's cap of 1% per month or the legal maximum, whichever is less. Additionally, the dispute window is only 7 days rather than a real dispute window before any finance charge applies (CD's standard uses 30 days), and there is no credit-extension-by-default provision if Hotel fails to send a credit application.
findings.cd_standard: Finance charges on a late, undisputed balance should be capped at 1% per month or the legal maximum, whichever is less; Group should have a real dispute window (30 days) before finance charges apply; and credit should be extended automatically if Hotel never sends or follows up on a credit application.
findings.proposed_language: Group will have thirty (30) days from receipt of the final itemized invoice to review and dispute any charge in good faith before any finance charge accrues on the disputed amount. Any amounts not paid within thirty (30) days of the due date on undisputed charges shall accrue a finance charge not to exceed one percent (1.0%) per month, or the maximum allowed by law, whichever is less. If Hotel fails to send Group a credit application, or fails to send a written reminder to complete it, Hotel will extend credit to Group.
findings.quoted_text:
Group shall have seven (7) days from receipt of each invoice to notify the Hotel in writing of any disputed charges; invoices not disputed within this seven (7) day window shall be deemed accepted by Group and shall be final and binding.

Payment of undisputed invoices shall be due within thirty (30) days of invoice date unless otherwise agreed in writing. Any amounts not paid within thirty (30) days of the due date shall accrue a monthly finance charge of two percent (2%) per month on the outstanding balance, compounded monthly, until paid in full.

findings.finding_text: The reservation cutoff is set at 30 days prior to arrival, and the block is stated to release in full at that time, rather than continuing to honor the group rate post-cutoff for as long as the hotel sells rooms to the general public, or holding/refunding unassigned rooms per Group's direction. Although 30 days exceeds CD's 21-day minimum floor (so the cutoff date timing itself is acceptable), the post-cutoff rate handling and full release of the block deviate from CD's standard.
findings.cd_standard: After cutoff, attendees should still get the group rate for as long as the hotel is selling rooms to the general public, and rooms still unassigned at cutoff should either be held for Group on prepayment, refunded if attendees later pay for them, or released for resale only after consultation with Group.
findings.proposed_language: After the cutoff date, Hotel will continue to hold any rooms in Group's block not assigned to a specific attendee if Group pays for them in full at that time, and will refund those advance payments after the Event for any such rooms later paid for by Group attendees; alternatively, after consultation with Group, Hotel will offer unassigned rooms to other individuals or groups to reduce any damages Group may owe under the attrition clause. Group members may continue to reserve rooms at the group rate for as long as Hotel is selling rooms to the general public, regardless of room type.
findings.quoted_text: Reservations for rooms within the Block must be submitted no later than thirty (30) days prior to the arrival date of April 26, 2027, unless a later deadline is expressly agreed in writing by the Hotel.

findings.finding_text: The contract contains no commission clause at all — no provision for ConferenceDirect's 10% commission on actualized room revenue, payment timing, non-cancelability, or commission on cancellation/attrition damages collected.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should pay ConferenceDirect 10% commission on all actualized room revenue, including rooms booked outside the block, miscoded rooms, walked rooms, and no-show/cancellation-fee room nights, within 30 days of departure, non-cancelable and non-transferable, plus 10% of any cancellation damages collected.
findings.proposed_language: All rates confirmed in this Agreement are commissionable at ten percent (10%) to ConferenceDirect, LLC. Hotel will pay commission to ConferenceDirect on all actualized room revenue, regardless of rate paid and including all rooms outside the block, within thirty (30) days of Group's departure, whether or not the master account has been paid in full. Commission for this booking is non-cancelable and non-transferable to another party or agency. Hotel will pay ConferenceDirect ten percent (10%) of any liquidated damages paid by Group within ten (10) days of receiving them.

findings.finding_text: There is no provision addressing what happens if the Hotel itself cancels the agreement outside of a permitted termination right — no obligation to pay Group's direct, indirect, or consequential damages such as costs of finding a replacement venue, rate/airfare differentials, or attorney's fees.
findings.cd_standard: If the hotel cancels the agreement without a right to do so under the contract, it should owe the group all direct, indirect, and consequential damages, not just a refund of deposits.
findings.proposed_language: In the event Hotel cancels this Agreement other than as permitted under this Agreement, Hotel will pay Group for all direct, indirect, and consequential damages, expenses, attorney's fees, and costs incurred by Group on account of such cancellation, including but not limited to staff time and travel expenses to secure an alternate location for the Event, incremental room rate and airfare differentials, function space rental, and long distance telephone, postage, and printing costs.

findings.finding_text: The contract does not name specific function rooms, minimum square footage, or ceiling heights, does not state whether room rental is waived, and does not commit to complimentary meeting space or in-room equipment (wired microphone, podium, power, lighting, HVAC) at no charge.
findings.cd_standard: The contract should name each function room with minimum square footage and ceiling height, restrict changes to the assignment without written consent, provide complimentary meeting space with room rental waived, and provide a wired microphone, podium, power, lighting, and HVAC at no charge.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will hold the meeting and function space set out in Exhibit [X] of this Agreement, with room rental charges waived, and will specify each function space assignment, minimum square footage, and ceiling height requirement. No change will be made to the function space assignments without the written consent of both parties. Hotel will provide in each meeting room, at no charge, one wired microphone, a podium, power, proper lighting, and HVAC.

findings.finding_text: There is no provision addressing what happens if the Hotel closes or materially reduces restaurants, spa, fitness facilities, meeting space, or staffing ratios — no offer of alternative facilities/services or Group's right to cancel or renegotiate if no alternative is reached.
findings.cd_standard: If the hotel closes or limits facilities/services by more than 25%, or materially reduces staffing ratios, it should first offer equal alternatives at its own expense, and Group should be able to cancel without liability or renegotiate if no alternative is reached within 30 days.
findings.proposed_language: If Hotel closes or limits the hours of service of any current restaurant, health club, spa, fitness facility, contracted meeting space, or other hospitality venue or facility by more than twenty-five percent (25%) of its published capacity or full-service offering, or materially reduces staffing ratios for housekeeping, food and beverage, banquet, engineering, or security services, Hotel will first have the option to provide equal alternative facilities or services at Hotel's expense. Should no mutually agreeable alternative be reached within thirty (30) days, Group may cancel this Agreement without liability, or the parties may instead modify this Agreement on mutually agreed terms.

findings.finding_text: The room rate of $372.00 appears fixed for this single event and there is no provision addressing a rate cap or downward adjustment mechanism should the market decline before arrival, though this may be less applicable given the rate is already confirmed for a single event year.
findings.cd_standard: Where room rates for a future year are not yet confirmed, the contract should cap increases at 2% per year and lower the group rate if market rates decline before arrival, with final rates fixed no later than 12 months before the event.
findings.proposed_language: Should the market average rate for same-tier hotels, or Hotel's published transient rate over the same pattern, decline between the signing of this Agreement and Group's arrival, the group rate will be discounted by the same percentage.

findings.finding_text: There is no nondiscrimination clause protecting attendees on the basis of sex, gender identity, race, disability, sexual orientation, and similar grounds, nor a termination right if state/local legislation permits such discrimination.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should commit that it and its staff will not discriminate against attendees on protected grounds even where state or federal law would allow it, with a termination right if legislation permits such discrimination.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel agrees that Hotel and its employees and agents will not discriminate against any of Group's attendees on the basis of sex, actual or perceived gender, age, race, color, religion, creed, national or ethnic origin, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, genetic information, or parental, marital, domestic partner, civil union, military, or veteran status, notwithstanding that such discrimination may be allowed under state or federal law. Should the state of California or the city of San Francisco adopt legislation that affirmatively allows discrimination on any of these bases, Group may terminate this Agreement without liability.

findings.finding_text: There is no provision addressing confirmation timing for individual reservations, name changes at the group rate up to arrival, individual room cancellation deadlines (6pm day of arrival), no-show reinstatement, or individual deposit refund timing/credit toward attrition.
findings.cd_standard: Confirmations should go out at no charge within 4 days, name changes allowed at the group rate up to arrival, individual cancellations free until 6pm day of arrival, no-shows reinstated the next night, and individual deposit refunds credited against attrition damages.
findings.proposed_language: Upon request, Hotel will send each registered guest confirmation of their reservation, and of any change to it, at no charge within four (4) days of receiving the information, or within two (2) business days if the request is received within thirty (30) days of arrival. Name changes may be made to room reservations at the group rate at any time up to and including the arrival date. No cancellation fee will be assessed for any room cancelled before 6:00 p.m. on the day of arrival. Hotel will reinstate no-shows for the following night at the rate of their existing reservation unless Group directs otherwise. Any individual reservation deposit will be refunded if notice of cancellation is received at least three (3) working days before arrival, and any individual cancellation money Hotel receives will be credited toward any attrition damages owed by Group.

findings.finding_text: There is no provision guaranteeing minimum server-to-guest or bartender-to-guest staffing ratios at food and beverage functions, or a cap on labor fees for small functions.
findings.cd_standard: The contract should guarantee minimum staffing ratios for plated and buffet meals and bartenders, with no labor/service fees for meeting those ratios and a labor fee only for functions under 25 people.
findings.proposed_language: At all meal functions, Hotel will provide at least one server for every twenty-five (25) guests at a plated breakfast and every twenty (20) guests at a plated lunch or dinner, and one server for every forty (40) guests at a buffet breakfast and every thirty (30) guests at a buffet lunch or dinner, with no extra service or labor charge for these ratios. At all functions where alcohol is served, Hotel will provide no fewer than one (1) bartender for every seventy-five (75) guests at hosted bars and one (1) bartender for every one hundred (100) guests at cash bars, with no bartender or service fees.

findings.finding_text: There is no reference to an attached AV or internet bandwidth quote, no minimum bandwidth commitment (10 Mbps down/1 Mbps up), and no discount for additional AV/internet needs added later.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should honor AV and internet bandwidth quotes attached at contracting, with bandwidth of at least 10 Mbps download and 1 Mbps upload, and a stated discount on later additions, without conditioning discounts on using the in-house AV provider.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will honor the pricing of the attached audio-visual quote, prepared from Group's specifications at the time of contracting, and will apply a discount of [X]% to any additional audio-visual needs, regardless of which provider is in place during the Event. Hotel will provide internet bandwidth of a minimum of 10 Mbps download and 1 Mbps upload speed, with a discount of [X]% on any additional needs. Use of Hotel's in-house audio-visual provider will not be a condition of any discounted or complimentary service, such as internet.

analysis.document_notes: The contract is a fairly comprehensive, well-drafted document overall, with several clauses (attrition threshold/formula, cancellation sliding scale, named storm, walk/relocation, mandatory fees disclosure, ADA, assignment, governing law/venue, damage deposit, attendee data, resale mitigation, labor disputes cancellation right, brand/ownership change notice, construction/renovation) already aligned with or close to CD's standard position and not flagged below. No exhibit A (cancellation damages schedule) or AV/internet quote exhibits were included in the text provided, though referenced — these should be requested and reviewed separately if available. No dollar exposure figures could be reliably calculated from the amounts given in most findings except where noted, since block size (230 peak rooms), F&B minimum, and per-vendor surcharge amounts were the only figures with sufficient specificity."

findings.finding_text: Attrition is measured night-by-night rather than cumulatively, with an 85% threshold (not 70%), and damages are based on the average actual/projected nightly rate rather than a defined single net group rate at 70% lost-profit factor applied only to genuinely unsold rooms. There is no audit right that is truly independent (occupancy records only, with a 30-day 'deemed acceptance' waiver), no F&B credit against attrition, and no rebate for a future ConferenceDirect rebooking. The 100% (not 95%) occupancy credit threshold is also stricter than CD's standard.
findings.cd_standard: Attrition liability should be measured cumulatively across the block, triggered only below 70% pickup, damages capped at 70% of lost profit on the single net group rate, with full-night credit at 95%+ occupancy, audit rights, and rebooking credit.
findings.proposed_language: Attrition liability, if any, will be calculated on a cumulative (not night-by-night) basis, with liability triggered only if Group's actual pickup falls below seventy percent (70%) of the total contracted room block. For each unsold room night below that threshold, Group will pay an amount equal to seventy percent (70%) (lost profit) of Group's single confirmed net group rate of $279.00 (plus tax, if required by applicable law), calculated as the lesser of the number of unsold rooms in the Hotel that night or the shortfall between Group's minimum block and actual pickup. For any night the Hotel achieves ninety-five percent (95%) occupancy or higher, Group will receive full credit toward its block commitment for that night. At Group's request, Hotel will provide a copy of its city ledger or daily report showing the information needed to verify the calculation, without any deadline-based waiver of Group's right to dispute. Any excess food and beverage revenue above Group's F&B minimum will be credited dollar for dollar against room attrition damages, and vice versa. Should a ConferenceDirect client rebook the Hotel for another meeting within three (3) years, Hotel will credit up to 100% of the attrition damages paid toward the new booking's room revenue.
findings.quoted_text: Attrition is measured on a night-by-night basis and applies to the total room nights committed by Group under this Agreement.
findings.exposure_basis: Depends on actual pickup shortfall; base rate $279/night across 930 committed room nights (465 rooms x avg nights), not calculable without pickup figures

findings.finding_text: Cancellation damages are calculated on gross room revenue rather than 70% lost-profit on net group rate, with a sliding scale reaching 80-90% (the table shows conflicting figures of 68%/81%/90% vs. the narrative's 20%/40%/60%/80%), well above CD's 100%-of-lost-profit ceiling. There is no rebooking credit for a future ConferenceDirect client, and the liability-free window (6 months / Feb 2, 2027) is a narrower carve-out than CD's standard sliding scale approach starting at close-in penalties only.
findings.cd_standard: Cancellation damages should be a disclosed sliding scale calculated on 70% lost room profit (not gross revenue) with mitigation credit and rebooking credit for future ConferenceDirect bookings.
findings.proposed_language: In the event of cancellation, liquidated damages will be calculated as a percentage of room profit — defined as seventy percent (70%) of the confirmed single net group rate of $279.00, multiplied by the final adjusted room block less allowable attrition — on the sliding scale stated in this Agreement, rather than as a percentage of gross room revenue. Should a ConferenceDirect client rebook the Hotel for another meeting within three (3) years, Hotel will credit up to 100% of the cancellation damages paid toward the new booking's room revenue.
findings.quoted_text: Group shall pay Hotel liquidated damages calculated as a percentage of gross room revenue as set forth herein.
findings.exposure_basis: 930 total committed room nights (465 peak x avg) x $279 x 90% (highest tier damages, close-in cancellation) approx.; illustrative upper-bound exposure under gross-revenue basis vs. CD's 70%-lost-profit standard

findings.finding_text: The narrative cancellation tiers (20%/40%/60%/80% at 180+/120-180/60-120/<60 days) conflict directly with the table's tiers (None/None/68%/81%/90%), creating ambiguity as to which schedule governs and both of which sit above CD's lost-profit-based approach.
findings.cd_standard: The dollar amount and percentage owed at each cancellation tier should be clearly and consistently disclosed in the agreement.
findings.proposed_language: Reconcile the narrative cancellation damages schedule and the table in Section 4 so that only one, internally consistent sliding scale applies, calculated on the 70% lost-profit basis described above.
findings.quoted_text: 180 through 91 days prior to arrival | 68%

findings.finding_text: Section 5 explicitly exempts the hotel's resale/mitigation records and process from any disclosure, audit, or review by Group, removing the ability to verify that mitigation actually occurred, contrary to CD's standard requiring documented, group-visible mitigation efforts.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should have a documented duty to mitigate by reselling canceled inventory, with records available to Group to verify the effort.
findings.proposed_language: The Hotel's resale efforts, including any attempts to place canceled rooms or space, its marketing activities, pricing decisions, and all related records and documentation shall be made available to Group upon reasonable request to verify that mitigation efforts were undertaken and that the rooms and space held for Group went unsold.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel's resale efforts, including any attempts to place canceled rooms or space, its marketing activities, pricing decisions, and all related records and documentation shall remain the sole property and responsibility of the Hotel and shall not be subject to disclosure to Group, audit by Group, or review by Group's representatives.

findings.finding_text: Force majeure requires performance to be physically impossible, not merely impracticable or inadvisable, and expressly excludes attendee safety concerns and travel reluctance absent a specific government order — narrower than CD's standard, which allows termination based on reasonable judgment of impracticability, inadvisability (including safety), or anticipated 20%+ attendee cancellations. There's also no provision for holding a smaller, reduced-size meeting with fee waivers, and a strict 10-day notice requirement to invoke force majeure is not in CD's standard.
findings.cd_standard: Either party should be able to cancel without liability when a cause beyond its control makes performance illegal, impossible, commercially impracticable, or inadvisable (including for health/safety), or would cause or lead Group to reasonably anticipate 20%+ attendee cancellations, without requiring an actual government order.
findings.proposed_language: Either party may cancel this Agreement without liability upon written notice to the other party should any cause beyond the control of Hotel or Group — including acts of God, war, terrorism, civil unrest, disease or epidemic, a CDC or governmental travel advisory, government closures or travel restrictions, or any other cause beyond the parties' control — in that party's reasonable judgment make it commercially impracticable, inadvisable (including from a health or safety standpoint), illegal, or impossible to perform, or cause or lead Group to reasonably anticipate that twenty percent (20%) or more of its attendees will cancel their attendance. If Group elects to hold a reduced-size Event, Hotel will waive attrition, food and beverage minimum, and function space rental fees related to the reduction, and offer Group's attendees any lower room rate offered to other guests.
findings.quoted_text: provided that performance has become physically impossible as a direct result of such cause and not merely more difficult, costly, or inconvenient

findings.finding_text: The termination-for-cause clause is a unilateral right reserved to the Hotel only, exercisable in Hotel's sole discretion, with no corresponding termination right for Group covering pandemic judgment, labor disputes, ownership/brand change, renovation, facility reduction, convention center unavailability, or discriminatory legislation as separate, no-liability grounds.
findings.cd_standard: Termination for cause should be available to Group, covering force majeure, Group's own pandemic judgment, labor disputes, ownership/brand/management change, renovation, facility reductions, convention center/overflow unavailability, and discriminatory legislation, entirely separate from the cancellation liquidated-damages scale.
findings.proposed_language: Group may terminate this Agreement without liability, and Hotel will refund all deposits and prepayments within five (5) days, upon any of the following: (a) force majeure; (b) Group's determination that an infectious disease outbreak, epidemic, or pandemic is affecting Group's ability to hold the Event as intended; (c) a labor dispute involving Hotel's employees arising within ninety (90) days of or during the Event; (d) a material change in Hotel's ownership, management company, or brand affiliation, or Hotel's bankruptcy or foreclosure; (e) renovation that Group determines will interfere with its meeting; (f) a reduction in Hotel's facilities or services for which no mutually agreeable alternative is reached within thirty (30) days; (g) unavailability of any convention center or overflow hotel on which the Event depends; or (h) adoption of state or local legislation permitting discrimination against attendees. None of the foregoing triggers the liquidated-damages calculation in the Cancellation clause.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel may terminate this Agreement immediately and without cause upon written notice to the Group if the Hotel determines in its sole discretion that circumstances render performance impossible or commercially impracticable.

findings.finding_text: A shortfall in F&B revenue is billed as the full dollar-for-dollar difference between actual charges and the minimum, rather than 35% of the gap as CD's standard requires; the 35% figure in the contract is instead used as a trigger threshold for the hotel to unilaterally renegotiate or add fees, not as the shortfall payment rate. There is also no provision counting affiliate/exhibitor F&B spend toward the minimum.
findings.cd_standard: Any F&B shortfall should be billed at 35% of the gap between actual revenue and the minimum, not the full difference, and affiliate/exhibitor F&B revenue should count toward the minimum.
findings.proposed_language: Should the Group's actual food and beverage charges fall short of the Minimum F&B Commitment, the Group shall pay Hotel thirty-five percent (35%) of the difference between actual revenue and the Minimum F&B Commitment, not the full shortfall. Food and beverage revenue from all affiliate organizations and exhibitors meeting in conjunction with Group's Event will count toward the Minimum F&B Commitment.
findings.quoted_text: the Group shall be obligated to pay the Hotel a shortfall fee equal to the difference between the Minimum F&B Commitment and the actual charges incurred
findings.exposure_basis: Depends on Event Summary's Minimum F&B Commitment amount, not stated in this document

findings.finding_text: The clause allows the Hotel to unilaterally introduce new fees and surcharges after execution without Group's written approval, binding Group to them automatically, directly contrary to CD's standard requiring Group's written approval before any post-signature charge is provided or posted. Additionally, the $26.00/night resort fee is not waived for attendees and there is no confirmation that resort-fee services are honored, nor any prohibition on early check-in or checked-bag fees.
findings.cd_standard: Later add-ons need the group's written approval before being provided or posted; resort fees should be waived for attendees (or discounted/fixed) while still honoring resort-fee services; no early check-in or checked-bag fees for attendees.
findings.proposed_language: Should Group require additional services or equipment after signature, Hotel must obtain Group's written approval before providing the service and before posting the charge to the master account. Hotel will waive the $26.00 nightly resort fee for all attendees while continuing to honor the resort fee services, will not charge attendees an early check-in fee when their room type is available, and will waive checked-bag fees for attendees arriving before check-in time or departing after check-out time.
findings.quoted_text: Hotel may, at its sole discretion and without prior notice to Group, introduce additional fees, surcharges, and service charges after this Agreement is executed, and all such charges shall be binding upon Group as modifications to the schedule of fees set forth herein.
findings.exposure_basis: $26/night resort fee x 465 rooms peak night x average nights not waived (5 nights x 186 avg rooms/night = 930 room-nights x $26 = $24,180); recalculated using 930 room nights

findings.finding_text: While the 1-per-40 complimentary room ratio matches CD's standard, the clause does not credit miscoded rooms or no-show/cancellation fee room-nights toward pickup for complimentary room calculation, and does not address complimentary in-room internet regardless of loyalty status.
findings.cd_standard: All occupied rooms should count toward pickup, including miscoded rooms and one room night per no-show/cancellation fee charged, and attendees should get complimentary in-room internet regardless of loyalty status.
findings.proposed_language: All occupied rooms will be counted toward Group's pickup for purposes of calculating complimentary rooms, including rooms credited to Group through a room block audit, and each no-show fee and cancellation fee charged will be credited as one (1) room night toward Group's pickup. Hotel will provide complimentary internet in attendees' guest rooms, regardless of brand loyalty program participation.
findings.quoted_text: Group shall receive complimentary room credit accruing at the ratio of one (1) complimentary room for every forty (40) paid rooms reserved and occupied by Group attendees during the Event Period

findings.finding_text: The cutoff date is set at 40 days prior to arrival rather than no earlier than 21 days, and reservations requested after the cutoff are not guaranteed the group rate for as long as the hotel sells to the public — they are only offered the rate 'subject to availability' at Hotel's discretion, and Group has no attrition-mitigation mechanism (holding rooms on prepayment or release after consultation).
findings.cd_standard: Cutoff should be no earlier than 21 days prior to arrival, with the group rate honored post-cutoff as long as the hotel is selling to the public, and unassigned rooms handled via prepayment-hold, refund, or consultative release.
findings.proposed_language: The cutoff date for the room block will be twenty-one (21) days prior to Group's major arrival date. After the cutoff date, Group members may continue to reserve rooms at the group rate for as long as Hotel is selling rooms to the general public, regardless of room type, and, once the block has sold, for as long as Hotel is selling the contracted room type to the general public. After consultation with Group, Hotel will offer unassigned rooms to other individuals or groups to reduce any damages Group may owe under the attrition clause.
findings.quoted_text: All reservations for rooms in the Group block must be requested and confirmed with Hotel no later than forty (40) days prior to the first date of the Event

findings.finding_text: The finance charge is set at 1.5% per month compounded monthly, exceeding CD's 1%-per-month (or legal maximum, whichever is less) cap, and there is no staged deposit schedule (25%/25%/50%) specified for Group if credit is denied — only an undefined Hotel-determined prepayment percentage.
findings.cd_standard: Finance charges on late, undisputed balances should be capped at 1% per month or the legal maximum, whichever is less; if credit is denied, Group should pay on a defined staged schedule (25% within 14 business days of denial, 25% one month out, 50% three days before event).
findings.proposed_language: Should Group fail to pay any undisputed invoice balance in full by the due date, Hotel shall assess a finance charge not to exceed one percent (1.0%) per month, or the maximum rate permitted by law, whichever is less. Where Group has not been approved for credit terms, Group will pay twenty-five percent (25%) of estimated charges within fourteen (14) business days of the credit denial, twenty-five percent (25%) one (1) month prior to the Event, and fifty percent (50%) three (3) days before the Event.
findings.quoted_text: the Hotel shall assess a finance charge of 1.5% per month, or the maximum rate permitted by law, whichever is lower, calculated on the unpaid principal balance and compounded monthly until payment is received in full

findings.finding_text: The $30,000 security deposit refund window is set at 45 days after checkout rather than the 30-day window CD's standard calls for, though the deposit is otherwise properly restricted to documented damage only.
findings.cd_standard: Any security or damage deposit should be refundable within 30 days absent documented damage.
findings.proposed_language: Any portion of the deposit not applied to documented damage claims shall be refunded to Group within thirty (30) days of Group's final checkout, provided all rooms have been inspected and the master account has been reconciled.
findings.quoted_text: Any portion of the deposit not applied to documented damage claims shall be refunded to Group within forty-five (45) days of Group's final checkout

findings.finding_text: Although drafted neutrally by referencing 'the state in which Group maintains its principal offices,' the clause specifies venue only in that state's courts without naming the city where Group is located, and while punitive damages and attorney's fees provisions match CD's standard, the venue provision should also specifically tie to the city where Group is located, not merely the state.
findings.cd_standard: Governing law and dispute venue should be the state and city where Group is located.
findings.proposed_language: This Agreement will be construed and interpreted in accordance with the laws of the state in which Group is located. Any unresolved controversy or claim arising out of or relating to this Agreement will be settled by a court of law in the city in which Group is located.
findings.quoted_text: exclusive jurisdiction and venue for any action or proceeding brought to enforce or interpret this Agreement shall lie in the state and federal courts of that state

findings.finding_text: Group's cancellation right for a labor dispute is conditioned on the dispute 'materially affecting the provision of services essential to the Event' and is subject to the Hotel's own determination that 'full Hotel services will be available,' giving the Hotel discretion to defeat Group's cancellation right — contrary to CD's standard, under which Group may cancel with no liability regardless of whether Hotel can still technically perform.
findings.cd_standard: If a strike, lockout, or expired union contract arises within 90 days of the event, Group should be able to cancel with no liability at all, regardless of whether Hotel can technically still perform.
findings.proposed_language: If, within ninety (90) days prior to or during the Event, Hotel's contract with its union employees has expired, picketing occurs, or a strike or lockout occurs, Group may cancel this Agreement by written notice without liability, regardless of whether Hotel is able to perform. This clause supersedes all other provisions of this Agreement.
findings.quoted_text: Group's right to cancel without liability under this clause shall not apply if the labor dispute is resolved to the satisfaction of Group and the Hotel determines that full Hotel services will be available for the Event dates

findings.finding_text: Auxiliary aid costs are to be 'shared' between the parties according to their respective legal obligations rather than the clear division CD's standard calls for — Group funding aids in its function space and Hotel funding aids in guest rooms/common areas.
findings.cd_standard: Group should fund auxiliary aids needed in the function space held for its use; Hotel should fund auxiliary aids required in guest rooms, public space, and common areas.
findings.proposed_language: Group is responsible for obtaining and funding any auxiliary aids needed in the function space held for its use; Hotel is responsible for obtaining and funding any auxiliary aids required by law in guest rooms, public space, and common areas. Both parties will communicate known auxiliary-aid and accessible-guest-room needs to the other in advance.
findings.quoted_text: the cost of such auxiliary aids shall be shared between the Hotel and the Group in accordance with the parties' respective legal obligations under applicable accessibility law

findings.finding_text: The contract does not specify function room square footage, ceiling height requirements, whether meeting room rental is waived/complimentary, or whether each room comes with a wired microphone, podium, power, lighting, and HVAC at no charge — Exhibit A only lists space names and estimated attendance, and function space is described as merely 'tentative' pending Hotel confirmation.
findings.cd_standard: The contract should name each function room with minimum square footage and ceiling height, no changes without both parties' written consent, complimentary meeting space with rental waived, and each room equipped at no charge with wired microphone, podium, power, lighting, and HVAC.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will hold the meeting and function space set out in Exhibit A, with room rental charges waived, and will specify each function space assignment's minimum square footage and ceiling height requirement. No change will be made to the function space assignments without the written consent of both parties. Hotel will provide in each meeting room, at no charge, one wired microphone, a podium, power, proper lighting, and HVAC.

findings.finding_text: The contract contains no guaranteed staffing ratios for servers or bartenders at food and beverage functions, and no cap limiting labor/service fees to only functions under 25 guests.
findings.cd_standard: The contract should guarantee minimum server-to-guest and bartender-to-guest staffing ratios with no extra labor charge for meeting them, and a labor fee only for small functions under 25 people.
findings.proposed_language: At all meal functions, Hotel will provide at least one server for every twenty-five (25) guests at a plated breakfast and every twenty (20) guests at a plated lunch or dinner, and one server for every forty (40) guests at a buffet breakfast and every thirty (30) guests at a buffet lunch or dinner, with no extra service or labor charge for these ratios. Hotel will provide no fewer than one (1) bartender for every seventy-five (75) guests at hosted bars and one (1) bartender for every one hundred (100) guests at cash bars, with no bartender or service fees. There will be no special labor or service fees for any Group food or beverage function, except that functions of fewer than twenty-five (25) people will incur a stated labor fee.

findings.finding_text: There is no attached audio-visual or internet bandwidth quote referenced or incorporated, no honored minimum bandwidth commitment, and no stated discount for AV/internet needs added after contracting.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should honor AV and internet bandwidth quotes attached at contracting (minimum 10 Mbps down/1 Mbps up), with a discount on later additions, and no linkage between in-house AV use and discounted/complimentary internet.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will honor the pricing of the attached audio-visual quote and will apply a discount of [X]% to any additional audio-visual needs, regardless of provider. Hotel will provide a minimum internet bandwidth of 10 Mbps download and 1 Mbps upload, with a discount of [X]% on any additional needs. Use of Hotel's in-house audio-visual provider will not be a condition of any discounted or complimentary service, such as internet.

findings.finding_text: The contract contains no provisions on reservation confirmation timing, name-change rights, individual cancellation deadlines (e.g., 6pm day-of-arrival), no-show reinstatement, or individual deposit refund timing.
findings.cd_standard: Reservation confirmations should go out within 4 days (2 business days inside 30 days of arrival), name changes at the group rate up to arrival, individual cancellation without charge until 6pm day of arrival, no-show reinstatement, and individual deposit refunds with 3 working days' notice, credited against attrition.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will send each registered guest confirmation of their reservation at no charge within four (4) days of receiving the information, or two (2) business days if within thirty (30) days of arrival. Name changes may be made at the group rate at any time up to and including the arrival date. No cancellation fee will be assessed for any room cancelled before 6:00 p.m. on the day of arrival. Hotel will reinstate no-shows for the following night at the rate of their existing reservation unless Group directs otherwise. Any individual reservation deposit will be refunded if notice of cancellation is received at least three (3) working days before arrival, and any individual cancellation money Hotel receives will be credited toward any attrition damages owed by Group.

findings.finding_text: The contract contains no commission clause for ConferenceDirect at all — no 10% commission on actualized room revenue, no timing for payment, and no protection for commission surviving rate adjustments, walked rooms, or brand/management changes.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should pay ConferenceDirect 10% commission on all actualized room revenue within 30 days of departure, non-cancelable, surviving brand/management change, including on cancellation damages collected.
findings.proposed_language: All rates confirmed in this Agreement are commissionable at ten percent (10%) to ConferenceDirect, LLC. Hotel will pay commission to ConferenceDirect on all actualized room revenue, regardless of rate paid and including all rooms outside the block, within thirty (30) days of Group's departure, whether or not the master account has been paid in full. Commission for this booking is non-cancelable and non-transferable. Hotel will pay ConferenceDirect ten percent (10%) of any liquidated damages paid by Group within ten (10) days of receiving them.

findings.finding_text: There is no provision requiring the Hotel to pay Group's direct, indirect, and consequential damages if the Hotel cancels the Agreement outside of a permitted termination-for-cause circumstance; the only Hotel-side termination mechanism is the one-sided 'Termination for Cause' clause discussed above, which merely triggers a deposit refund.
findings.cd_standard: If the hotel cancels without a contractual right to do so, it should owe Group all direct, indirect, and consequential damages, not just a refund of deposits.
findings.proposed_language: In the event Hotel cancels this Agreement other than as permitted under this Agreement, Hotel will pay Group for all direct, indirect, and consequential damages, expenses, attorney's fees, and costs incurred by Group on account of such cancellation, including but not limited to staff time and travel expenses to secure an alternate location for the Event, incremental room rate and airfare differentials, function space rental, and long distance telephone, postage, and printing costs.

findings.finding_text: There is no provision addressing the Hotel's closure or material reduction of restaurants, spa, fitness facilities, or staffing ratios, and no corresponding right for Group to cancel or renegotiate if no alternative is reached.
findings.cd_standard: If the hotel closes or limits any facility by more than 25% or materially reduces staffing ratios, it should first offer equal alternatives; if no agreement is reached within 30 days, Group should be able to cancel without liability or renegotiate.
findings.proposed_language: If Hotel closes or limits the hours of service of any current restaurant, health club, spa, fitness facility, contracted meeting space, or other hospitality venue by more than twenty-five percent (25%) of its published capacity or full-service offering, or materially reduces the guest-to-staff service ratio of its housekeeping, restaurant, banquet, maintenance and engineering, or safety and security services, Hotel will first offer equal alternative facilities or services at its own expense. Should no mutually agreeable alternative be reached within thirty (30) days, Group may cancel this Agreement without liability, or the parties may modify this Agreement on mutually agreed terms.

findings.finding_text: Room rates for the event are already fixed in this contract at $279.00, so a future-year rate cap may not be directly applicable, but there is no clause addressing a rate decrease pass-through if market rates fall before arrival, which CD's standard calls for as a floor protection.
findings.cd_standard: The group rate should be lowered if the market average rate for comparable hotels or the hotel's own published rate declines before arrival.
findings.proposed_language: Should the market average rate for same-tier hotels, or Hotel's published transient rate over the same pattern, decline between the signing of this Agreement and Group's arrival, the group rate will be discounted by the same percentage.

findings.finding_text: The contract contains no nondiscrimination commitment for attendees and no termination right tied to discriminatory state or local legislation.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should commit that it and its staff will not discriminate against attendees on protected grounds, and Group should be able to terminate without liability if state/local legislation allows such discrimination.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel agrees that Hotel and its employees and agents will not discriminate against any of Group's attendees on the basis of sex, actual or perceived gender, age, race, color, religion, creed, national or ethnic origin, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, genetic information, or parental, marital, domestic partner, civil union, military, or veteran status. Should the state of Washington or the city of Seattle adopt legislation that affirmatively allows discrimination on any of these bases, Group may terminate this Agreement without liability.

analysis.document_notes: The Cancellation clause (Section 4) contains an internal inconsistency between the narrative tiers (20%/40%/60%/80% at 180+/120-180/60-120/<60 days) and the accompanying table (None/None/68%/81%/90% at overlapping but differently-labeled bands), which should be clarified with the property before relying on either schedule. The Attrition clause references a nightly-rate calculation methodology using 'average of actual rates' rather than a fixed single net group rate, complicating exposure calculations. Exposure dollar amounts for attrition, F&B minimum shortfall, and mandatory fee waiver were only calculable where base figures (room rate, block size, resort fee) were explicit in the body text; other clauses (e.g., F&B minimum dollar amount) are deferred to an unattached 'Event Summary' not included in this document, so exposure could not be quantified there.
